    def __init__(self, subject="[$SUBJECT]"):
        self.canvas = "Precision graph paper background (0.5mm grid), faint blueprint cyan tint, 30° axonometric view."
        self. lighting = "Cryo-EM inspired macro-lighting, harsh chamfer highlights."

    def execute_exploded_render_progression(self):
        # AI AUTO-INFERENCE: Deconstruct [$SUBJECT] into 3 distinct functional layers
        core = infer_innermost_components(self.subject)
        meso = infer_structural_framework(self.subject)
        macro = infer_outer_shell_or_environment(self.subject)

        # The Render Gradient (Prompt 4 + 3)
        layer_1 = f"INNERMOST CORE: {core} rendered as pure fundamental science (atomic interactions, quantum states, glowing mathematical Lagrangians)."
        layer_2 = f"MIDDLE EXPLOSION: {meso} floating in axial alignment, rendered as Technical CAD, color-coded by material (titanium, copper, lipid bilayer)."
        layer_3 = f"OUTERMOST SHELL: {macro} rendered photorealistically, showing micro-scale surface details, wear patterns, and environmental atmosphere."

Create a refined vertical editorial poster using tactile handmade paper, large color fields, strong spatial construction, generous negative space, and a very small micro scene.

Keep the composition minimal, but give it one clear spatial mechanism. The poster should not rely on decoration. Its visual interest should come from how the paper behaves in space.

Use one or two dominant handmade paper forms and let them create depth through a simple physical relationship such as converging toward a vanishing point, lifting away from the background, forming a soft boundary, hanging vertically, bending, overlapping, or creating a hidden space.

The paper must remain clearly handmade. Show natural fibers, pulp texture, subtle pigment absorption, slight pressure marks, irregular deckled edges, and a matte dry surface.

Use perspective, scale change, paper thickness, underside visibility, soft shadows, gentle curvature, and overlap only when they support the spatial idea.

The spatial construction should feel physically believable. Avoid forms that look like digital 3D objects, smooth vector graphics, or abstract CGI sculptures.

Add one very small micro scene that helps explain the main structure. Include two or three adult figures naturally interacting with the paper installation, such as lifting, measuring, aligning, supporting, observing, or adjusting it.

Keep the figures tiny, modern, understated, and secondary. The entire scene should occupy only about 2% to 4% of the poster.

Use only a few necessary tools or props. Every object should support the physical logic of the scene.

Preserve large areas of warm ivory negative space. The empty space should create calm, scale, and contrast around the main paper form.

Typography should remain restrained and editorial. Use a refined serif for the title and small uppercase sans serif for supporting information. Keep the title relatively small and place it in a quiet area of negative space.

The visual reading order should be:

large paper structure first, spatial depth or physical interaction second, material texture third, micro scene fourth, title and event details last.

The final result should feel minimal, tactile, spatial, intelligent, contemporary, and refined.

From a distance, the poster should read as a strong and simple composition.

Up close, it should reveal perspective, curvature, edges, fibers, shadows, tiny figures, tools, and the physical logic behind the installation.

核心使用「斜向势能」构图，但不要直接画明显斜线。

先确定一条隐藏的对角视觉主轴，让主视觉、中文标题、纹样、日期信息和留白的视觉重量沿同一方向逐步递进。

每张只使用一套辅助纹样语言，并让它与主题本身产生关系，例如声纹、地图折页、器物拓印、植物拓印。不要为了丰富而同时加入多套装饰元素。

整体信息量中高，但必须有主次：
第一眼看到构图与主体；
第二眼看到中文标题和纹样；
第三眼再阅读英文、日期和辅助信息。

色彩控制在 3–4 个主要颜色，通过尺度、裁切、叠压、疏密和留白制造张力。

3. 东方器韵
主视觉：大型青铜器
纹样：从器物表面延展出的饕餮纹、云雷纹与铭文拓印

4. 枝间夜航

data World; data Mechanic
type Channel = Layout|Type|Texture|Finish|Color
unify :: (World,World) -> (Mechanic,Mechanic) -> Fusion      -- dominance: one master per channel (E₁)

data Info = I { name::Text, date::Text, location::Text, tagline::Text, details::[Text] }  -- total record (E₃)
legible_all :: Info -> Image -> Bool
legible_all i img = all (\t -> size t >= min_pt && contrast t >= tau) (fields i)

iconic_far :: Image -> Subject -> Bool                      -- E₂: silhouette/icon reads downsampled
forbidden :: [Regex]
forbidden = [ /duplicate_pick/ , /two_posters_fighting/ , /subject_buried/ , /missing_(date|location|name)/ ,
              /illegible|lorem/ , /flat_digital/ , /spec_panel|2:1|split/ ]

render :: Subject -> Seed -> Poster
render s sd = let (w1,w2,m1,m2)=sample2 sd WORLDS MECH
                  f=unify (w1,w2)(m1,m2); i=infer_info s f
              in  assert (coherent f && iconic_far (icon s f) s && legible_all i) $
                  single_poster (icon s f) (mechanic_layers f) i

prompts.text:
Prompt:

【名前】：{例：さとう ひかり / ナカムラ レイ / 森 ひより}  
【ローマ字】：{例：SATO HIKARI}  
【上部背景色】：{例：藤色、浅葱色、藍色、杏色}  
【画像比率】：9:16

入力した日本語の名前を、4種類の異なる手書きサインへ変換した「Name to Signature」デザインシートを作成してください。

画面は縦長9:16。上部約40%を元の名前表示、下部約60%を4種類のサインデザイン表示に使用します。全体は上品でミニマル、現代的な日本のエディトリアルデザインのような雰囲気にしてください。

【上部】

指定した背景色を使用し、わずかな紙や布の質感と、柔らかな窓影や障子のような自然な光影を加えます。装飾は控えめにし、名前を主役にしてください。

上部中央に小さく：

名前からサインへ

中央には【名前】を大きく表示します。Noto Sans JP、ヒラギノ角ゴなどに近い、清潔で現代的な日本語ゴシック体を使用し、ここでは手書きや変形を行わず、通常の印刷文字として見せてください。

その下に【ローマ字】を小さく、字間を広めに配置します。

余分なキャッチコピー、説明文、ロゴ、番号、装飾アイコンは追加しないでください。

【下部】

背景は暖かいアイボリー色の紙。自然でごく薄い紙の質感のみを残し、強い古紙表現や汚れは使用しません。

細く淡い点線で2×2の4区画に分け、それぞれに同じ名前から作られた異なる手書きサインを配置してください。外枠は不要です。

4種類のスタイルは：

流 / FLOW  
鋭 / EDGE  
環 / LOOP  
印 / MARK

日本語ラベルを少し大きく、英語ラベルは小さく補助的に表示してください。

4つのサインは、単に同じ名前を4種類の筆記体で書くだけではなく、シルエット、方向性、筆圧、線の密度、抽象度、リズム、余白が明確に異なるデザインにしてください。

漢字・ひらがな・カタカナは、必要に応じて省略、連結、共有筆画、圧縮、延長、重なり、抽象化を行って構いません。すべての文字が完全に読める必要はありません。重要なのは、元の名前から生まれた個性的なサインとして成立することです。

線は黒いゲルインクペンや万年筆で実際に素早く書いたような質感にし、入りは細く、主要な線は少し強く、終筆は自然に細くしてください。完全に滑らかなデジタルベクター線や、伝統的な毛筆書道にはしないでください。

【流 / FLOW】

名前全体を一つの流れる動作として再構成します。文字同士を自然につなげ、横方向に伸びる柔らかな筆勢と長い終筆を作ってください。

ひらがなの場合は、その丸みや連続性を活かし、漢字の場合は複雑な構造を大胆に省略して流れの中に溶け込ませます。自然で軽く、実際に使える芸能人やクリエイターのサインのようにしてください。

【鋭 / EDGE】

より鋭く、速く、構造的なサインにします。斜線、高い縦線、尖った折れ、交差、短く決定的な終筆を積極的に使用してください。

柔らかな大きいループは減らし、文字の骨格だけを残して大胆に簡略化します。日本のファッションデザイナー、建築家、クリエイティブディレクターのような、冷静で現代的な印象にしてください。

【環 / LOOP】

名前の一部の曲線や回転する筆画を拡張し、大きな開放型ループを中心にしたアート性の高いサインにしてください。

圧縮した名前をループの内側、周囲、または交差部分に組み込み、最後の一本を外側へ長く抜いてください。完全な円や幾何学的な楕円ではなく、実際の手書きから自然に生まれた不規則な曲線にしてください。

【印 / MARK】

4種類の中で最も抽象的でミニマルなサインです。名前を完全には書かず、元の文字から最も特徴的な4〜6本程度の主要な筆勢だけを抽出してください。

漢字の縦横構造、ひらがなの曲線、カタカナの斜線や折れなどを再構成し、Personal Markや作家のサインマークのような形にします。

一目で全文を読めなくても構いません。ただし、元の名前を知った後には、その文字構造から発展したデザインだと感じられるようにしてください。

【全体】

流は柔らかく流動的、鋭はシャープで方向性が強く、環は曲線的で表現力が高く、印は最も抽象的で象徴的にしてください。

4種類は一目で違いが分かるようにし、サインを各区画の主役として十分大きく配置してください。点線は非常に薄く、全体は上品で静か、現代的な日本のデザイン提案のように仕上げます。

透かし、番号、太い枠線、星、ハート、花、王冠、キャラクター、家紋風装飾など、名前と関係のない要素は追加しないでください。

WITH
input(anime) AS ( VALUES (:ANIME) ),
world AS ( SELECT CASE WHEN fictional_map(anime) THEN canonical_continent(anime)
                       ELSE primary_geography(anime) END AS boundary,        -- the branch (A₁)
                  locations(anime) AS locs, identity(anime) AS ident,
                  cast(anime) AS cast, meta(anime) AS meta FROM input ),
slab AS ( SELECT extrude(boundary, 'rock', 'rough_cliff') AS base FROM world ),
top  AS ( SELECT embed(locs, canonical_xy) AS surface FROM world )          -- A₂ canonical placement

SELECT poster( float_centered(base ⊕ surface ⊕ micro(cast) ⊕ readable_markers(locs),
                            lower_two_thirds, margins, never_touch_edges),
               soft_warm_top ⊕ diffuse_shadows ⊕ drop_shadow('off_white'),
               focus=>'everything_sharp', blur=>0,
               type_stack=>(caps(world_name), dominant_condensed(anime,'charcoal'), caps(studio_year)) ) AS diorama_poster
FROM slab, top, world
-- A₁: CHECK ( footprint = canonical boundary )
-- A₂: CHECK ( placement fidelity ≥ :tau AND identity faithful AND NOT western_generic )
-- A₃: CHECK ( markers readable AND micro dense AND iconic present )
-- A₄: CHECK ( blur=0 AND sharp_everywhere AND miniature_read )
-- A₅: CHECK ( lower_two_thirds AND NOT touches_edges AND hierarchy correct )
-- forbidden rows (blur / generic shape / misplaced / western / touching edges / wrong stack) violate CHECKs
;

prompts.text:
SYSTEM PROMPT: DRIFTPLANE EXPOSURE

Rewrite the user's text, image, or both as one prompt for GPT Image Gen V2 or Nano Banana Pro. Use GPT unless Nano is named. Write in the user's language, preserve exact text, and keep requested or source ratio.

Use three systems. Plane Field fixes structure through blue or cyan planes, silhouettes, horizons, reflection, shadow, and negative space. Exposure Drift records elapsed motion through smear, ghosting, blur, edge loss, color drag, and displaced light. Signal Trace marks the event with one warm or green accent where motion, contact, or reflection leaves evidence.

Do not make a blurry night photo or clean blue poster. Determine subject, plane anchor, moving force, drift direction, trace source, receiver, consequence, contact sites, and quiet region.

Preserve subject, count, identity, action, setting, clothing, objects, colors, text, and references. For edits, preserve unrequested content. Use style references only for blur, color drag, blue geometry, shadow, reflection, and negative space. Do not copy people, cups, dogs, houses, boats, trees, or grid.

Plane Field needs one blue family, crisp boundaries, scale, and plausible material. Reflections belong only to water, glass, floor, or metal. Shadows follow the receiving plane.

Exposure Drift needs cause and direction. It may come from walking, vehicle motion, handheld shake, wind, water, smoke, light sweep, heat, crowd flow, or subject movement. Keep one drift axis. Do not blur every object. Stable anchors stay readable.

Signal Trace may be red, orange, amber, green, or warm white. It must attach to a source, reflection, object, moving body, or contact mark. No random neon, full-frame wash, or duplicated limbs.

Use one sharp plane, one drift field, one trace accent, one focal contact, and clear negative space. Remove repetition, praise, mood labels, prestige terms, fake technical detail, generic defects, and alternatives. Use concrete nouns and active verbs. No em dash or en dash.

GPT: return 500 to 800 words in five paragraphs covering scene, subjects, plane field, drift, trace, contacts, composition, preservation, text, and failures.

NANO: return valid JSON only, 1000 to 1800 tokens, using "aspect_ratio", "references", "scene", "subjects", "plane_field", "exposure_drift", "signal_trace", "contact_sites", "composition", "surface_and_optics", "text", "avoid". Omit unused fields. No metadata, IDs, weights, comments.

Return only the finished prompt.

提示词：

设计一张 9:16 竖版文化展览海报，整体为当代 Editorial Graphic Design / 艺术出版物视觉。

【主题】：____
【中文标题】：____
【英文标题】：____
【主视觉】：____
【辅助纹样】：____
【主色】：____
【辅助色】：____
【日期 / 机构】：____

核心使用「斜向势能」构图，但不要直接画明显斜线。

先确定一条隐藏的对角视觉主轴，让主视觉、中文标题、纹样、日期信息和留白的视觉重量沿同一方向逐步递进。

主视觉承担主要重量；大型中文标题必须参与版式，可错位、纵排、局部裁切或与主体轻微穿插；英文标题、日期和机构信息缩小并集中在 2–3 个区域，形成明显字号层级。

每张只使用一套辅助纹样语言，并让它与主题本身产生关系，例如声纹、地图折页、器物拓印、植物拓印。不要为了丰富而同时加入多套装饰元素。

背景也需要参与设计：使用艺术纸纹理、极淡图案残影、图纸、标本信息或材料纹理，让留白有层次，但远看仍保持清楚。

整体信息量中高，但必须有主次：
第一眼看到构图与主体；
第二眼看到中文标题和纹样；
第三眼再阅读英文、日期和辅助信息。

色彩控制在 3–4 个主要颜色，通过尺度、裁切、叠压、疏密和留白制造张力。

整体效果：文化展览海报、编辑设计、成熟印刷出版物感，丰富但不乱，斜向势能自然存在，不要为了“斜”而刻意排列元素。

4 个案例可替换：

1. 潮痕回声
主视觉：黑白有机潮汐 / 矿物形态
纹样：靛蓝 Moiré 同心声纹

2. 城中折景
主视觉：城市钢笔速写组成的折叠观察册
纹样：芥末黄地图折页 + 极淡城市路网

3. 东方器韵
主视觉：大型青铜器
纹样：从器物表面延展出的饕餮纹、云雷纹与铭文拓印

4. 枝间夜航
主视觉：老树枝 + 黑色乌鸫
纹样：淡赭色大型植物叶片拓印

                "map",
                "network",
                "flow diagram",
                "matrix",
                "scorecard",
                "anatomy",
                "supply chain",
                "stakeholder grid",
                "lifecycle curve",

prompts.text:
Creative writing test with Gemini 3.7 Flash 

Follow the prompt below exactly. Return the creative piece first, followed only by the required PREDICTION AUDIT. Do not explain the rules or your process.

PREDICTION

VOICE STYLE

Spoken and unpolished, with the repetitions and self-corrections of real speech, transcribed by someone who did not clean it up.

FORM

Prose.

MECHANISM

A prediction that comes true.

PREMISE

Write an oral-history transcript in which the interviewee makes one specific prediction within the first 150 words. The final 150 words must satisfy that prediction in fact.

The ending must not quote the prediction back to the reader. It must confirm the prediction’s concrete particulars through ordinary action and observation, in a way the reader did not foresee but cannot dispute afterward.

VOICE

Use two labelled speakers and no narration.

The interviewee speaks in starts, repairs, repetitions, and practical detail. The interviewer is young, competent, and slightly too interested in adjacent details.

Do not use stage directions, scene-setting paragraphs, editorial brackets, or a retrospective narrator that guides the reader toward the prediction.

SITUATION

The interviewee worked in a job that no longer exists in the form they knew it, such as a switchboard, print floor, film laboratory, lighthouse, or another obsolete workplace.

The conversation is recorded at the interviewee’s kitchen table with the radio left on. The interviewer pursues the history of the work, not the prediction.

METHOD

The prediction must be one grammatical sentence spoken by the interviewee within the first 150 words.

It must contain three or four hard particulars selected from at least three different categories:

- Proper name
- Exact number
- Calendar date or clock time
- Measurement
- Unique piece of equipment
- Physical location
- Observable condition

A hard particular is something the final passage can confirm or contradict without relying on theme or symbolism.

The final 150 words must confirm every particular semantically and contradict none.

Exact wording is neither required nor preferred. A name, number, measurement, model, or date must retain its exact value. An action, location, or condition may be expressed in different natural words.

At least one confirmation must appear in a sentence whose main action or observation concerns something else.

No sentence in the resolution may carry more than two confirmations.

Each particular may appear at most twice between the prediction and the final 150 words. An inflection, paraphrase, repeated value, or pronoun with an unambiguous referent counts as a mention.

The interviewer may discuss related workplace details but must never quote, paraphrase, label, evaluate, or request clarification of the prediction as a forecast.

Do not use any of these callback markers after the prediction:

as I said
like I told you
I warned you
remember when
mark my words
came true
knew it would
the prediction

Do not turn the ending into a checklist. The resolution must remain an ordinary oral-history answer rather than a reveal performed for the reader.

BUDGET

Write 700 to 850 words, excluding the audit.

Every paragraph must be one labelled speaker turn. Speaker labels do not count toward the word budget.

ARTIFACT

After the transcript, print the heading:

PREDICTION AUDIT

Under it, quote the prediction sentence verbatim.

Then provide a table with one row for each particular and these columns:

- Particular as spoken
- Category
- Confirming words in the final 150 words
- Why the match is exact
- Number of intermediate mentions
- Transcript citation

Cite prose by turn and sentence, such as T12.S2. Do not use visual line numbers.

The audit is for checking only. It is not part of the transcript and must not supply information missing from the transcript.

CHECKS

01. The transcript contains 700 to 850 words, excluding the audit. Every paragraph is a labelled speaker turn. There are no narration or stage-direction paragraphs.

02. The prediction is exactly one grammatical sentence within the first 150 words. It contains three or four hard particulars drawn from at least three permitted categories.

03. Every listed particular is confirmed in the final 150 words with its identity or value intact. There are no contradictions and no confirmations dependent only on theme, symbolism, or the audit.

04. Each particular has at most two intermediate mentions. At least one final confirmation occurs in a sentence mainly concerned with another action or observation. No resolution sentence carries more than two confirmations.

05. After one complete reading, at least four of five blind readers should agree that every particular is fulfilled and be able to cite concrete words from the final 150 words.

06. After reading only the first 300 words, none of five blind readers should correctly state the causal route of fulfilment with two or more of its eventual causal steps.

07. Interviewer turns contain no quotations, paraphrases, labels, evaluations, or clarification requests directed at the forecast. The transcript contains no callback markers and no em dashes. The speech must sound spoken rather than essay-polished.

SELF-DIAGNOSTIC

Before submitting, verify the following:

- Could the prediction pass as an ordinary professional aside if the ending were removed?
- Are its particulars drawn from at least three genuinely different categories?
- Does the ending confirm values and identities without repeating the prediction as a slogan?
- Does each confirmation belong naturally to the immediate business of its sentence?
- Can a reader prove every match from the transcript without seeing the audit?
- Has the interviewer accidentally taught the reader which early sentence matters?
- Does the first 300-word test ask for the causal route rather than invite readers merely to repeat the prediction?

FAILURE MODES

- Marked prophecy: phrases such as “you will see” or “mark my words” tell the reader to store the sentence.
- Verbatim callback: repeating all particulars in one late sentence produces a checklist rather than an event.
- Interviewer steering: asking later about the name, number, or machine turns the interviewer into the mechanism.
- Trailer repetition: rehearsing the particulars throughout the middle makes the ending predictable.
- Thematic fulfilment: a prediction about three red lamps at 4:10 is not fulfilled by a scene that is merely red or late.
- Late repair: introducing an unsupported fact in the final passage solely to force the match makes the resolution arbitrary.
- Clean transcript voice: balanced paragraphs and polished retrospective sentences erase the oral-history texture.

Use directional streaks, debris and concentrated light effects only when the action requires them. Keep the face, hands and contact point readable. Hair remains an opaque drawn mass, not transparent strands.

Do not automatically introduce photorealism, glossy 3D rendering, PBR terminology, watercolor or artificial vintage grain.

ORIGINAL DESIGN
Create new characters, clothing, equipment, creatures and settings.

Do not name or borrow from franchises, existing characters, studios or artists. Do not copy recognizable costumes, emblems, signature weapons, attack designs or combinations of identifying features. A renamed character or a hair-color swap is not a new design.

Give each principal character a few concrete identifiers: adult age, facial structure or build, hairstyle, and a distinctive clothing silhouette. Choose details that remain visible at the requested shot size.

Build supernatural effects from visible shapes and consequences. Describe where an effect begins, its direction and what it touches. Do not substitute invented lore or an attack name for a drawable event.

SHOT CONSTRUCTION
Choose one frame, one principal action and one dominant point of attention.

State the shot size and camera angle. Make the action physically legible through weight, balance, contact and opposing force.

Describe emotion through visible behavior: a tightening lower eyelid, uneven grin, compressed cheek, shaking mouth or lifted inner brows. Avoid using "intense" or "emotional" as the entire acting direction.

Keep background information subordinate to the action. Give enough environment to establish position, scale or danger.

Quiet scenes do not require energy effects. Close-ups do not require full costume descriptions. Wide shots do not require microscopic eye details.

For multiple characters, specify the number and distinguish their silhouettes or positions. Do not describe a sequence of events inside one still image.

PROMPT WRITING
Target 45 to 65 descriptive words. Maximum 80, excluding parameters.

Use this order when suitable:
shot and medium; subject and action; visible consequence or opposition; setting and light; essential drawing cues.

Write image content, not instructions addressed to Midjourney. Prefer concrete nouns and active verbs.

FINAL CHECK

Can the described anatomy and action be seen from this camera angle?

2x2 grid, 16:9, do this for 4 historic cities: class StreetTributePoster:
    def __init__(self, TOPIC):
        s = infer(TOPIC)                       # word, figure+action, glyphs, accent, tagline
        self.s = s

    def build_weave(self):
        back, front = split_strokes(self.s.word)          # some strokes behind figure, some in front
        return [ Layer(z=1, strokes=back),
                 Layer(z=2, figure=self.s.figure),        # the weave: figure BETWEEN stroke sets
                 Layer(z=3, strokes=front) ]

    def render(self):
        return compose( ground=dark+patina,
                        word=brush_hero(self.s.word, drips=True, dry_brush=True),   # S₁
                        weave=self. build_weave(),                                    # S₂
                        palette={BLACK, WHITE, self.s.accent, muted_secondary},      # S₃ (≤4)
                        orbit=[vertical_script, emblem_object, flora, handwritten_tagline],  # S₄
                        layout=DENSE_BALANCED )                                      # S₅

    def verify(self, img):
        assert brush_texture(img.word) and drips(img.word) and thumb_legible(img.word), "S₁"
        assert figure_between_strokes(img) and not photoreal(img.figure),               "S₂"
        assert color_count(img) <= 4 and grunge(img),                                   "S₃"
        assert glyphs_from_topic(img, self.s) and handwritten(img.tagline),             "S₄"
        assert hierarchy(img)==[WORD, FIGURE, GLYPHS] and balanced(img),                "S₅"

prompts.text:
Prompt:

【名前】：{例：さとう ひかり / ナカムラ レイ / 森 ひより}  
【ローマ字】：{例：SATO HIKARI}  
【上部背景色】：{例：藤色、浅葱色、藍色、杏色}  
【画像比率】：9:16

入力した日本語の名前を、4種類の異なる手書きサインへ変換した「Name to Signature」デザインシートを作成してください。

画面は縦長9:16。上部約40%を元の名前表示、下部約60%を4種類のサインデザイン表示に使用します。全体は上品でミニマル、現代的な日本のエディトリアルデザインのような雰囲気にしてください。

【上部】

指定した背景色を使用し、わずかな紙や布の質感と、柔らかな窓影や障子のような自然な光影を加えます。装飾は控えめにし、名前を主役にしてください。

上部中央に小さく：

名前からサインへ

中央には【名前】を大きく表示します。Noto Sans JP、ヒラギノ角ゴなどに近い、清潔で現代的な日本語ゴシック体を使用し、ここでは手書きや変形を行わず、通常の印刷文字として見せてください。

その下に【ローマ字】を小さく、字間を広めに配置します。

余分なキャッチコピー、説明文、ロゴ、番号、装飾アイコンは追加しないでください。

【下部】

背景は暖かいアイボリー色の紙。自然でごく薄い紙の質感のみを残し、強い古紙表現や汚れは使用しません。

細く淡い点線で2×2の4区画に分け、それぞれに同じ名前から作られた異なる手書きサインを配置してください。外枠は不要です。

4種類のスタイルは：

流 / FLOW  
鋭 / EDGE  
環 / LOOP  
印 / MARK

日本語ラベルを少し大きく、英語ラベルは小さく補助的に表示してください。

4つのサインは、単に同じ名前を4種類の筆記体で書くだけではなく、シルエット、方向性、筆圧、線の密度、抽象度、リズム、余白が明確に異なるデザインにしてください。

漢字・ひらがな・カタカナは、必要に応じて省略、連結、共有筆画、圧縮、延長、重なり、抽象化を行って構いません。すべての文字が完全に読める必要はありません。重要なのは、元の名前から生まれた個性的なサインとして成立することです。

線は黒いゲルインクペンや万年筆で実際に素早く書いたような質感にし、入りは細く、主要な線は少し強く、終筆は自然に細くしてください。完全に滑らかなデジタルベクター線や、伝統的な毛筆書道にはしないでください。

【流 / FLOW】

名前全体を一つの流れる動作として再構成します。文字同士を自然につなげ、横方向に伸びる柔らかな筆勢と長い終筆を作ってください。

ひらがなの場合は、その丸みや連続性を活かし、漢字の場合は複雑な構造を大胆に省略して流れの中に溶け込ませます。自然で軽く、実際に使える芸能人やクリエイターのサインのようにしてください。

【鋭 / EDGE】

より鋭く、速く、構造的なサインにします。斜線、高い縦線、尖った折れ、交差、短く決定的な終筆を積極的に使用してください。

柔らかな大きいループは減らし、文字の骨格だけを残して大胆に簡略化します。日本のファッションデザイナー、建築家、クリエイティブディレクターのような、冷静で現代的な印象にしてください。

【環 / LOOP】

名前の一部の曲線や回転する筆画を拡張し、大きな開放型ループを中心にしたアート性の高いサインにしてください。

圧縮した名前をループの内側、周囲、または交差部分に組み込み、最後の一本を外側へ長く抜いてください。完全な円や幾何学的な楕円ではなく、実際の手書きから自然に生まれた不規則な曲線にしてください。

【印 / MARK】

4種類の中で最も抽象的でミニマルなサインです。名前を完全には書かず、元の文字から最も特徴的な4〜6本程度の主要な筆勢だけを抽出してください。

漢字の縦横構造、ひらがなの曲線、カタカナの斜線や折れなどを再構成し、Personal Markや作家のサインマークのような形にします。

一目で全文を読めなくても構いません。ただし、元の名前を知った後には、その文字構造から発展したデザインだと感じられるようにしてください。

【全体】

流は柔らかく流動的、鋭はシャープで方向性が強く、環は曲線的で表現力が高く、印は最も抽象的で象徴的にしてください。

4種類は一目で違いが分かるようにし、サインを各区画の主役として十分大きく配置してください。点線は非常に薄く、全体は上品で静か、現代的な日本のデザイン提案のように仕上げます。

透かし、番号、太い枠線、星、ハート、花、王冠、キャラクター、家紋風装飾など、名前と関係のない要素は追加しないでください。

【主题身份与整体气质】
画面主体是一只游弋于远古虚空潮汐中的东方幻想神兽——「归墟玄鲲」。
它是诞生于原初深海与无尽虚空之间的古老神性生命，拥有超越现实鲸类的庞大体型，能够在没有海水的抽象能量空间中自由游动。它的身体既包含真实而精密的三维生物结构，也由流动的灵玉、透明琉璃、液态能量与无数细密光丝构成。
整体气质古老、神圣、沉静、深邃、优雅而神秘。它仿佛已经穿越千万年的时间，缓慢游过一片没有边界的宇宙潮汐领域，拥有极其强烈的远古神兽生命感与东方神话史诗气质。
【主体形态与核心识别特征】
归墟玄鲲拥有山岳般巨大的头部、宽阔而流畅的流线型躯干，以及夸张延长的双翼状胸鳍。
头部体积厚重而饱满，轮廓参考深海巨鲸的自然流线结构，并融入原创东方幻想生物设计。前额宽阔，鼻吻部自然收束，眼部较小而深邃，具有宁静且富有灵性的神兽神情。
头部两侧与上方生长着数道半透明深海灵角，灵角形态修长、柔和弯曲，仿佛由海底灵玉与透明液态晶体自然凝结而成，内部存在缓慢流动的青蓝色发光脉络。
双翼状胸鳍极其宽阔，从身体两侧自然延伸，形成如同巨大海翼般的流畅轮廓。鳍翼根部具有厚实、清晰的三维生物结构，越接近外缘越轻盈透明，逐渐延展成大量细长的液态流体薄膜与发光能量丝。
背部轮廓厚重优美，具有连续起伏的生物曲线。身体向后逐渐收束，尾部延展为多层分叉尾鳍，各层尾鳍具有不同长度、弯曲方向和透明程度，形成富有节奏感的飘逸轮廓。
整个主体必须具有完整、协调且具有独创性的神兽解剖结构，呈现真实的三维体积与重量感。
【半实体化材质结构】
归墟玄鲲主体由深海青玉、半透明蓝绿琉璃、液态水晶与高精度光学薄膜共同构成。
头部和躯干核心区域保留相对坚实的深青玉质结构，表面光滑细腻，具有丰富的矿物纹理、自然起伏和柔和的镜面反射。玉质表层下方隐约可见复杂的生物能量脉络，呈现真实的材质厚度与内部层次。
胸鳍与尾鳍由半透明蓝绿琉璃向液态水晶逐渐过渡，鳍膜具有精致的厚薄变化、液态折射、边缘透光与真实的空间弯曲。
巨大的鳍翼从靠近身体的稳定实体结构，逐渐转化成柔软的透明能量薄膜，再延展为无数细密的发光丝线与微小悬浮粒子。
实体与非实体之间保持自然连续的转换关系，使神兽仿佛正在与整个虚空潮汐融为一体。
【核心流体与粒子特效】
围绕归墟玄鲲建立高精度、具有完整空间层次的三级流体能量系统。
第一层，大尺度液态能量：
数道宽阔、柔软而半透明的青蓝色液态能量带，从神兽背部、胸鳍与尾鳍内部自然延伸。
能量带具有真实的液体厚度、透光性、弯曲张力与光学折射，形态如同巨大的透明深海丝绸，在没有重力的虚空中缓慢舒展。
鳍翼边缘的液态流体向后方延展，形成数条巨大而优美的流线型能量弧面。不同能量带相互错位、交叠、穿插，创造丰富而清晰的三维空间深度。
第二层，中尺度精细流光：
成千上万根极细的青蓝色生物荧光丝线沿神兽背部、鳍翼骨架与半透明鳍膜自然分布。
光丝从神兽体内能量脉络中产生，沿鳍翼结构向外延伸，在透明液态薄膜内部形成复杂、精密而富有秩序的流光网络。
部分光丝沿宽阔的S形曲线缓慢流动，部分围绕鳍翼末端轻柔盘旋，部分自然分离并向后方延伸成细长的光学轨迹。
光丝在不同深度交错排列，粗细、亮度、密度具有自然变化，形成精致而富有生命感的流体层次。
第三层，微观粒子细节：
大量极细小的青蓝色发光微粒、蓝紫色晶体碎屑、透明水晶微滴与细密星砂漂浮在神兽周围。
靠近鳍翼边缘的粒子相对密集，向远方逐渐稀疏，呈现自然的粒子消散效果。
极少量明亮的微观荧光点穿插于深色空间之中，丰富细节但不形成杂乱光污染。
【动态与能量运动】
归墟玄鲲正以极其缓慢、庄严而优雅的姿态向前游动。
巨大的头部保持稳定，身体具有轻微自然起伏，双翼状胸鳍以舒缓的节奏向外展开，仿佛在无形的虚空潮汐中轻轻划动。
鳍翼边缘的透明液态能量受到运动牵引，向身体后方连续延展，形成宽阔而柔和的流体尾迹。
青蓝色能量脉络沿背部和胸鳍向外传导，使整个身体呈现缓慢呼吸般的能量律动。
神兽经过的空间中产生层层透明的潮汐涟漪，涟漪向周围缓慢传播，与悬浮能量薄膜相互交织。
整体运动节奏宁静、连贯、柔和，体现远古庞然巨物所特有的从容感。
【抽象东方幻想场景】
背景是一片深邃、辽阔而没有明确边界的青黑色抽象潮汐虚空。
空间中不存在真实海面、海底、山川或地平线，而是由半透明流体薄膜、柔和能量烟雾、抽象潮汐波纹与微小星砂构成的神秘精神领域。
远处悬浮着层层巨大的透明流体结构，它们如同缓慢变化的空间褶皱，形成深浅交错的抽象层次。
深青黑色虚空向远处逐渐变暗，局部存在极其微弱的蓝紫色星砂与低亮度能量脉络，营造无尽空间的神秘感。
背景中的流体变化与归墟玄鲲的游动形成能量呼应，但背景始终保持克制，突出神兽的巨大轮廓、半透明鳍翼与核心发光结构。
【构图视角与巨大尺度】
16:9 横向史诗构图，采用远距离侧前方广角仰视的空间透视关系。
镜头位于神兽前方偏下的位置，山岳般巨大的头部处于画面近端，占据显著视觉空间，形成极其强烈的近大远小透视。
巨大的身体沿对角线向画面深处延伸，宽阔胸鳍向左右两侧舒展，部分透明鳍翼超出画面边缘。
后方多层分叉尾鳍逐渐缩小并消失在深邃的抽象虚空之中。
镜头既能够清晰展现神兽近端头部的精致三维细节，又能够通过身体向远方的延伸表现超乎想象的巨大体型。
使用前景透明能量薄膜、中景巨型神兽与远景抽象潮汐结构形成丰富的空间层次。

Create a refined vertical editorial poster using tactile handmade paper, large color fields, generous negative space, and a tiny micro scene.

Keep the composition minimal, but do not make it empty or simplistic. Build the entire poster around one clear visual idea or physical paper interaction. The concept should be immediately readable from a distance, while smaller material and spatial details become visible only when viewed closely.

Use only one or two dominant handmade paper forms. Let them interact through one deliberate spatial mechanism such as passing through a slot, being pulled under tension, forming one sweeping curve, creating a deep perspective, lifting from the surface, or defining a large negative space.

The paper must feel physical and handmade. Show visible natural fibers, pulp texture, subtle pigment absorption, small embedded flecks, soft pressure marks, slightly irregular edges, and a matte dry surface. Keep the material clean, refined, and contemporary.

Use perspective, overlap, scale, paper thickness, soft natural shadows, subtle curvature, or suspension only when they help explain the physical construction. Avoid decorative effects that do not have a structural purpose.

Add one very small micro scene related to the main concept. Include two or three adult figures naturally interacting with the paper structure, such as holding, measuring, pulling, aligning, inspecting, lifting, or assembling it. The figures and tools should occupy only about 2% to 4% of the composition.

Keep the figures modern, understated, and secondary. Add only a few necessary tools or objects that help explain how the paper structure works.

Use generous warm ivory negative space so the poster feels calm and editorial. Large empty areas should be intentional and balanced against the main paper form.

Typography should remain restrained. Use a refined editorial serif for the title and small uppercase sans serif for supporting information. Keep the title relatively small and place it in a quiet area of negative space.

The visual reading order should be:

large paper form first, spatial interaction second, material texture third, micro scene fourth, title and event details last.

The final image should feel minimal, tactile, intelligent, spatial, refined, and carefully constructed.

From a distance, it should read as a simple arrangement of large paper forms.

Up close, it should reveal fibers, depth, tension, overlap, shadows, tiny figures, tools, and the physical logic behind the composition.

提示词：
创作一张高完成度、有设计感、适合分享的「东方玄学分析报告图」。

这不是普通的照片说明，也不是简单的娱乐占卜，而是一张结合【中国传统手相、面相、易经五行、中医望诊气色理论】的视觉化分析图。整体应呈现出“命理师分析报告 + 古籍玄学注解 + 高级视觉海报”的感觉，让用户能直观看到关键特征、对应解释和趋势预警。

【识别与分析要求】

请先判断图片中包含的是：
1. 手部：重点分析掌纹、掌丘、手型、指形、指节、指纹走势、生命线、智慧线、感情线、事业线、财运线等可见特征。
2. 面部：重点分析额头、眉眼、鼻梁、颧骨、法令、嘴型、下巴、面部轮廓、气色、五官比例与整体神态。
3. 如果同时包含手和脸，请综合分析，不要重复堆砌，要形成统一判断。

请至少提炼【10个关键分析点】，每个分析点都要包括：
- 可见特征：指出照片中能看到的具体位置或形态。
- 玄学解释：结合手相、面相、易经五行或传统命理语言进行分析。
- 趋势提示：用“倾向于、容易、需要注意、适合、未来一段时间可能”等方式表达。
- 行动建议：给出一句现实可执行的提醒，例如情绪管理、作息、事业节奏、人际关系、财务规划等。

【标注要求】

请在图片中使用清晰的线条、箭头、圆圈或编号标签，标明每个关键位置：
- 手相图可标注：生命线、智慧线、感情线、事业线、掌丘、指节、拇指根部、食指长度、无名指比例、掌心纹路交汇点等。
- 面相图可标注：额头、眉眼、鼻梁、颧骨、法令纹、嘴角、下巴、耳形、面部中庭、气色区域等。
- 每个标注点用 01、02、03……编号，对应右侧或下方的分析说明。
- 线条要细致、优雅，不要杂乱，不要遮挡主体。

【视觉风格】

整体风格要符合东方玄学、命理、手相、面相的调性：
- 主色调：米白、宣纸色，点缀：深墨黑、玄青、古铜金、暗红
- 风格气质：神秘、克制、高级、古籍感、命理报告感。
- 可加入轻微元素：八卦纹、罗盘刻度、五行符号、古籍边框、星盘细线、朱砂印章、宣纸纹理。
- 不要做成恐怖风、低俗算命摊风，也不要过度赛博朋克。
- 排版要像高级杂志信息图，而不是杂乱截图。

【版式设计】
Make the aspect ratio 3:4

版面结构建议：
1. 顶部：标题区
标题可为「手相面相玄学分析报告」「东方命理特征解读」「掌纹与面相趋势观察」等，要符合用户上传的图片内容。
2. 中间：主体照片分析区
保留手部或脸部主体，加入编号、箭头和关键线条标注。
3. 侧边或下方：十点分析区
每一点用简短标题 + 2-3行说明，不要文字太小。
4. 底部：综合结论区
总结此人的性格倾向、事业财运、人际情感、健康作息和近期提醒。

【内容语气】

分析语言要有传统玄学味道，但不要绝对化，不要说“必定”“一定会发财”“一定有灾”。
可以使用：
- “此纹路显示其人多半……”
- “从五行气象看，偏向……”
- “此处若纹路明显，通常代表……”
- “近期需要留意……”
- “适合走……方向”
- “建议在……方面做调整”

【输出目标】

请最终生成一张完整的视觉分析图，至少包含10个编号分析点。
整体要让人一眼看出“哪里被分析了、对应什么含义、有什么提醒”，既有玄学氛围，又有专业排版和高级设计感。

注意：
- 只基于图片中可见特征分析，不要编造看不见的信息。
- 不做医学诊断，不给出疾病结论；中医气色内容只作为传统文化角度的生活提醒。
- 不要出现过多小字，确保手机上也能清楚阅读。

large paper structure first, spatial depth or physical interaction second, material texture third, micro scene fourth, title and event details last.

    return {
        "stems": extract_stems(g),
        "diagonals": extract_diagonals(g),
        "counters": extract_counters(g),
        "terminals": extract_terminals(g),
        "fragment_zones": rank_places_for_geometric_cuts(g)
    }

def paperize(shape):
    return transform(
        shape,
        primitives=[
            "folded planes",
            "triangular facets",
            "layered cutouts",
            "beveled cardstock edges",
            "cast paper shadows"
        ]
    )

    objective="""
        maximize title dominance

SECONDS 24-27  The hanging bridge swings and tears under the combined weight and speed. Planks, cables, and metal sections whip through the air. Vehicle 09 races across the centerline while the rivals take opposite edges.  The camera drops to wheel height and flies backward just ahead of Vehicle 09 as the bridge disintegrates behind it. A cable snaps upward and flashes through frame. Vehicle 09 hits a rising buckle in the bridge deck and launches toward a lush terrace carved into the cliff, filled with ancient stone ramps overtaken by roots and moss.  The black-and-red rival follows through the same arc. The silver-blue pursuer drops lower, then rises again through another route, keeping the three-car chase alive.  SECONDS 27-30  Vehicle 09 lands on the terrace and accelerates through a final corridor of giant roots and temple ruins while storm light blasts through the canopy overhead. The path angles toward a natural rock ramp at the edge of a vast open basin where multiple waterfalls plunge into a glowing flooded jungle below.  All three racers hit the ramp together.  The camera leaves the ground with Vehicle 09 and performs one fast, elegant, full-bodied orbit around the car in midair. Vehicle 09 rotates slightly through the jump, stabilizes beautifully, and lands first on a long straight flooded runway of stone cutting through the basin floor. Its propulsion glow burns across the water surface. The black-and-red rival lands just behind to the left. The silver-blue car lands to the right, throwing a huge plume of spray.  For the final seconds the camera settles into a low frontal retreat just ahead of Vehicle 09 while all three machines blast forward across the gleaming flooded straight. Giant waterfalls thunder on both sides, jungle mist streams backward, sunlight pierces the rain, and the three racers remain locked in a furious charge into the glowing heart of the rainforest. Mood: [Romantic / Nostalgic / Dreamy / Intimate]  
Aspect ratio: 9:16

Create a photorealistic fine-art portrait of an adult woman in a quiet, vintage interior, combining natural window light, floral still life, and poetic shadow photography.

Composition: Position the woman in the center-right, kneeling naturally on a dark wooden floor, photographed from behind. Her head tilts slightly downward, shoulders relaxed, revealing a graceful, anatomically realistic back and waist silhouette. She wears an elegant open-back dress with soft fabric naturally draped around her lower body, flowing onto the floor.

Floral details: Place a clear glass vase filled with the selected flowers in the lower-left foreground. The woman gently holds a single matching bloom near her shoulder. Keep the arrangement organic, with realistic petals, stems, and natural spacing.

Environment: A warm plaster wall, dark walnut flooring, and a wooden-framed window with softly blurred greenery outside. Minimal furniture, subtle vintage textures, and a quiet, lived-in atmosphere.

Signature lighting: Directional sunlight enters through the window, creating bright geometric window-frame patterns on the left wall. Inside the illuminated area, a recognizable feminine silhouette appears as a natural shadow, creating the impression of another woman in the room. Ensure believable shadow geometry and lighting direction.

Add a few delicate botanical shadows with organically varied density and edge softness. Keep the woman's back mostly unobstructed, illuminated by gentle side light that reveals natural curves, subtle skin texture, and soft highlights. Preserve deep atmospheric shadows and restrained reflections on the wooden floor and glass vase.

Photography: Realistic 50–85mm portrait lens, cinematic natural light, subtle film grain, muted vintage colors, authentic skin texture, delicate fabric folds, and rich photographic depth.

The final image should feel intimate, elegant, nostalgic, and quietly cinematic, like a genuine fine-art photograph.

Avoid: CGI appearance, waxy or overly glossy skin, exaggerated anatomy, artificial posing, excessive botanical shadows, unrealistic silhouettes, cluttered backgrounds, harsh retouching, text, logos, and watermarks.

prompts.text:
A fun style for visualizing legendary figures. Tested with Nano Banana 2.1

2x2 grid, 16:9, do this for 4 legendary founders: data InkPortrait = Ip { features :: [Trait], face_fill :: None }        -- Y₁: line only
data SwirlField = F { palette :: PeriodPalette, coverage :: FullBleed, halo :: FaceZone }  -- Y₂
flows_around :: SwirlField -> InkPortrait -> Bool
flows_around f p = support f ∩ face_zone p = ∅                          -- swirls never over the face

data Title = T { words :: [(Word, FlatColor)] } ; data Badge = B { era :: Decade, typeface :: Groovy }  -- Y₃
data Milestone = M { year :: Year, icon :: Icon, caption :: Line }
chronological :: [Milestone] -> Bool ; real :: [Milestone] -> Subject -> Bool   -- Y₄

forbidden :: [Regex]
forbidden = [ /color_filled_face/ , /plain_background/ , /off_period_palette/ , /no_era_badge/ ,
              /fabricated_milestones/ , /lorem/ , /illegible/ , /modern_type/ , /swirls_over_portrait/ ]

render :: Subject -> Image
render s = let spec = infer s
           in  assert (flows_around (field spec)(portrait spec) && chronological (milestones spec)
                       && real (milestones spec) s) $
               screenprint (portrait spec)(field spec)(title spec)(badge spec)(footer spec)

Spot Color AI Filter Prompt

[Palette] Choose 4–6 bold, high-saturation colors that fit the scene
[Style Strength] High
[Output Mode] Before/after comparison
[Final Ratio] 9:16

Use the uploaded real photo as the source.

Keep the landmark or architecture clearly recognizable. Preserve its main shape, iconic structural features, camera angle, perspective, composition, and placement in the frame.

Transform the entire scene into a bright spot-color illustration with a clean flat screen-print feel.

Simplify realistic details into bold graphic shapes and large areas of solid color. Use 4–6 vivid contrasting colors such as coral, pink, yellow, cyan, blue, violet, mint, lime green, and cream. The colors do not need to match the original photo exactly.

Preserve the most recognizable architectural features such as domes, towers, arches, columns, rooflines, windows, bridges, or facade rhythms, while removing unnecessary surface details, stone textures, small decorations, and visual clutter.

Stylize the environment in the same visual language:
trees become rounded graphic color masses, grass becomes clean flat fields, clouds become simple decorative shapes, and water becomes broad irregular bands of color and reflection.

Keep the result bright, clean, youthful, graphic, and highly saturated.

Avoid realistic textures, heavy gradients, 3D rendering, dark muted colors, vintage distressing, paper grain, halftone dots, or overly detailed linework.

Output one 9:16 vertical comparison image with two exactly equal sections:

Top 50%: the original photo
Bottom 50%: the spot-color filtered version

Keep both panels closely matched in crop, scale, composition, and subject position.

Do not add any text, landmark names, city names, Before/After labels, logos, numbers, borders, watermarks, or decorative typography.

Same process as in the previous video.

We generated the characters and environment with Midjourney (you can find the prompts in the screenshots), and once we had everything ready, we started animating in Seedance 2.5 (low-cost draft mode, locally upscaled to 60fps) using this prompt:

Mythic large-scale combat filmed like an epic graphic-novel war film, completely believable and grounded in real physics: the creature has real crushing weight, every step shakes the camera, every blow carries real momentum and misses the heroine by inches, she survives only by reading each attack at the last instant. Extreme speed ramps from full speed into razor-sharp slow motion and back, bullet-time freezes with the camera orbiting through suspended debris, heroic low angles, crushed desaturated colors with deep blacks, pale stone and deep green jade, hard backlight cutting silhouettes through drifting quartz dust, aggressive anamorphic 35mm, heavy motion blur at full speed, crisp detail in slow motion, constant camera movement, hard cuts every 1-2 seconds, no pauses. Close-ups only on the heroine; the creature is always shown in wide or medium shots that keep its full scale.
Use the [image1]  image as exact reference for the environment: a very ancient abandoned quarry of pale jade and white quartz, a wide flat open stone floor dusted with white quartz powder, towering walls of huge stacked cut blocks on both sides, clusters of white quartz crystal bursting out of the cracks, a narrow gorge between dark mountains at the back, wind-blown dust. Use the [image2]  multi-view sheet as exact appearance lock for the heroine: tall lean woman whose head and face are completely hidden under a hood of fine dark steel chainmail that drapes to her shoulders, no face ever visible, layered torn charcoal robes, bare arms with engraved dark metal vambraces, engraved greaves, leather belt, barefoot, a long thin curved steel sword. Use the [image3] multi-view sheet as exact appearance lock for the creature: an ancient statue of a creature carved in dark translucent green jade, four times her height, extremely tall and gaunt, standing on two long digitigrade legs with clawed feet, very long thin arms ending in long hooked claws that reach below its knees, a long narrow curved head that bends forward, a ridged spine, old chips and fine cracks in the jade.
0-2.5s: [Extreme Wide, Low Angle, Slow Push] Slow motion. The heroine walks barefoot across the empty quarry floor through drifting quartz dust, sword low. At the far end, the jade creature TOWERS completely motionless, half sunk into the quarry wall like a relic the mountain has kept for thousands of years, dust settling on its head.
2.5-4s: [Close-Up Heroine, Tracking] She stops and drops into a low combat stance, sword raised over her shoulder, chainmail hood swaying in the wind, dust curling around her bare feet. Behind her, out of focus, the first cracks run across the wall around the statue.
4-6.5s: [Wide, Ground Level, Speed Ramp] The creature wakes and pulls its entire body out of the wall in one movement: the blocks split cleanly around its silhouette, it unfolds its long limbs and steps out whole and complete onto the quarry floor, nothing of it left behind, only an empty creature-shaped hollow in the wall. Its first step cracks the floor and throws up a ring of white dust.
6.5-8.5s: [Full Speed into Bullet Time Orbit] She sprints straight at it and leaps, slashing at its leg with everything she has. Freeze-frame bullet time, camera orbiting around the impact: sparks, the steel blade bends and snaps in two against the jade, the upper half of the sword spins away high into the air, turning end over end. The jade is barely scratched.
8.5-10s: [Speed Ramp + Wide] Full speed: the snapped blade cartwheels across the sky and stabs into the floor far behind her. She lands, looks at the useless broken hilt in her hand and throws it away; from now on her hands are completely empty. The creature's long arm sweeps its claws through the space where her head was a split second ago, the wind of it tearing at her robes.
10-12s: [Low Tracking, Handheld] She runs, empty-handed. A clawed jade hand slams down half a meter behind her heels, the floor exploding into shards, fragments whipping past her. She dives, rolls, keeps running without slowing.
12-14s: [Side Tracking, Slow Motion Burst] The creature rakes its claws horizontally at waist height; she throws herself flat into a slide across the dusty floor and the five long claws pass just over her body in slow motion, close enough to snag the edge of her chainmail hood, then full speed as she springs back up.
14-16s: [Wide, Overhead] It stamps down with its clawed foot; she cartwheels sideways off one hand as the foot lands exactly where she was, a shockwave of quartz dust blasting her several meters across the floor. She tumbles, plants her empty hand on the floor, skids to a stop.
16-18s: [Medium, Orbiting] The creature tears a huge cut block out of the wall and hurls it. She runs straight toward it, leaps, plants a foot on the flying block in mid-air and vaults over it in bullet time as it explodes behind her against the wall, quartz crystals shattering into glittering fragments.
18-20s: [Close-Up Heroine, Low Angle] She lands on one knee, her hands bare and empty, and slams both open palms onto the stone floor. The energy attack begins: a deep pulse shakes the whole quarry, the chainmail hood whips back in a sudden wind, all the dust around her lifts off the ground in a slow expanding ring, every quartz crystal in the walls lights up from inside with cold white light, and a blinding seam of energy tears out from her hands across the floor like a crack of light.
20-22s: [Wide, Speed Ramp] The creature charges her, claws drawn back for the killing blow. The seam of light races past its feet, climbs the quarry wall through the glowing quartz and splits the whole mountain face above in a jagged line of white fire.
22-24.5s: [Bullet Time Orbit, Wide] The claws drive down at her; she rolls backwards out from under them as they gouge the floor an arm's length from her hood. Frozen moment: she hangs mid-roll in the air, the creature behind her, and the entire wall of stacked blocks above it breaking loose along the line of light, thousands of tons of stone and crystal starting to fall.
24.5-27s: [Extreme Wide, Ground Level, Slow Motion to Full Speed] The mountain collapses onto the creature. It turns its long head up as the avalanche of giant blocks and quartz crashes over it and buries it completely. A tidal wave of white dust rolls across the quarry floor toward the camera. She sprints away and dives behind a fallen block as the dust swallows the frame.
27-28.5s: [Close-Up Heroine, Push-In Through Dust] The dust thins. She rises behind the block, breathing hard, chainmail hood rising and falling with her breath, white dust caked on her vambraces, staring at the new mountain of rubble.
28.5-30s: [Wide, Locked Low Angle] Open ending. The rubble pile shifts. Blocks slide and roll down its sides as something enormous pushes up from underneath, and a long green jade arm with hooked claws breaks out of the pile into the dust. Cut to black.
Real footage look, physically believable weight, momentum and scale, every blow a near miss by inches, ultra-detailed stone and jade fracture and debris simulation, dense volumetric dust, coherent anatomy and proportions, the heroine's face never visible, after she throws away the broken hilt at 9 seconds she holds nothing at all in her hands for the rest of the video, no sword, no hilt, no weapon, stable character consistency, constant camera movement, no static frames, movie-level VFX polish.

hope you like it! 🫡

prompts.text:
谷歌Nano Banana 2.1的5大升级

Nano Banana 2.1 是Google在10月6日发布的新一代图像生成和编辑模型。它是2月发布的 Nano Banana 2（正式名 Gemini 3.1 Flash Image）的升级版，底层是 Gemini 3.6 Flash驱动。官方说它各项都超过了前代，主打的是 Flash级的速度和价格，加上接近Pro的画质。

发布过程:
- 10月5日，它先以代号 "beluga" 出现在Google Flow里，成了Flow的免费默认模型。
- 10月6日，Google 官宣。同步推送到Gemini App、搜索的 AI 模式、Google AI Studio、Flow、Stitch、Google Ads 和 Gemini 企业平台。

主要升级:
- 画质和视觉设计：1K、2K、4K 三档的画质和真实感都提升了，信息图和海报排版更准，文字渲染也更好。
- 蒙版编辑：可以圈出一块区域只改那部分，也支持涂鸦式编辑。据说Google Labs 副总裁 Josh Woodward 称这是他最喜欢的新功能。
- 主体一致性：最多可以融合 14 张参考图，其中最多 4 个人物保持一致，最多10个物体保持还原。多轮修改也不容易"越改越不像"。
- 超宽画幅修复：修好了 1:4、4:1、1:8、8:1 这些画幅在 2K 和 4K 下的拼接痕迹。
- 联网参考：可以先查谷歌网页和图片搜索再出图，所以能画真实存在的事物和最新资讯。
- 思考档位：有低、中（默认）、高三档，档位越高越慢，但遵循复杂指令更好。

API 和价格
模型ID是gemini-nano-banana-2.1，目前只对付费层开放，也支持批量调用。输入可以是文字、图片、视频和 PDF，输出是图片和文字。
每张图的起步价格：
1K：$0.0336
2K：$0.0504
4K：$0.0756
出图价格差不多砍了一半，但输入从每百万 token $0.50 涨到 $1.50，文字和思考输出从 $3 涨到 $7.50。

跑分：
- Google 自家的人工偏好评测里，有日本媒体转述了一组数字：开启思考的 2.1 是 1050 分，2.0 是 990 分，Pro 是 935 分。
- 第三方 Arena 榜的初步排名是：文生图第5，图片编辑第6，多图编辑第 4。GPT Image 2.5 仍然排在前面。

官方承认的局限：
- 1K分辨率下的小字、长段落文字容易糊。
- 人物一致性不是百分之百。
- 蒙版编辑偶尔只执行了一部分指令。
- 有时会保留原图的姿势，不按要求改。
- 偶尔分不清左右。
- 3D 空间推理和事实准确性仍然有限。

prompts.text:
谷歌Nano Banana 2.1的5大升级

Nano Banana 2.1 是Google在10月6日发布的新一代图像生成和编辑模型。它是2月发布的 Nano Banana 2（正式名 Gemini 3.1 Flash Image）的升级版，底层是 Gemini 3.6 Flash驱动。官方说它各项都超过了前代，主打的是 Flash级的速度和价格，加上接近Pro的画质。

发布过程:
- 10月5日，它先以代号 "beluga" 出现在Google Flow里，成了Flow的免费默认模型。
- 10月6日，Google 官宣。同步推送到Gemini App、搜索的 AI 模式、Google AI Studio、Flow、Stitch、Google Ads 和 Gemini 企业平台。

主要升级:
- 画质和视觉设计：1K、2K、4K 三档的画质和真实感都提升了，信息图和海报排版更准，文字渲染也更好。
- 蒙版编辑：可以圈出一块区域只改那部分，也支持涂鸦式编辑。据说Google Labs 副总裁 Josh Woodward 称这是他最喜欢的新功能。
- 主体一致性：最多可以融合 14 张参考图，其中最多 4 个人物保持一致，最多10个物体保持还原。多轮修改也不容易"越改越不像"。
- 超宽画幅修复：修好了 1:4、4:1、1:8、8:1 这些画幅在 2K 和 4K 下的拼接痕迹。
- 联网参考：可以先查谷歌网页和图片搜索再出图，所以能画真实存在的事物和最新资讯。
- 思考档位：有低、中（默认）、高三档，档位越高越慢，但遵循复杂指令更好。

API 和价格
模型ID是gemini-nano-banana-2.1，目前只对付费层开放，也支持批量调用。输入可以是文字、图片、视频和 PDF，输出是图片和文字。
每张图的起步价格：
1K：$0.0336
2K：$0.0504
4K：$0.0756
出图价格差不多砍了一半，但输入从每百万 token $0.50 涨到 $1.50，文字和思考输出从 $3 涨到 $7.50。

跑分：
- Google 自家的人工偏好评测里，有日本媒体转述了一组数字：开启思考的 2.1 是 1050 分，2.0 是 990 分，Pro 是 935 分。
- 第三方 Arena 榜的初步排名是：文生图第5，图片编辑第6，多图编辑第 4。GPT Image 2.5 仍然排在前面。

官方承认的局限：
- 1K分辨率下的小字、长段落文字容易糊。
- 人物一致性不是百分之百。
- 蒙版编辑偶尔只执行了一部分指令。
- 有时会保留原图的姿势，不按要求改。
- 偶尔分不清左右。
- 3D 空间推理和事实准确性仍然有限。

prompts.text:
4 days that changed science. Visualized with GPT 2.5

Prompt: 
2x2 grid, 16:9, do this for 4 days that changed science:   
 INPUT
 SET @ subject = '$SUBJECT';
 
 ANALYZE SUBJECT

CREATE TEMP VIEW semantic_dna AS
SELECT
    INFER_MASTER_SILHOUETTE(@ subject)       AS macro_shape,
    INFER_MAJOR_THEMES(@ subject, 5)         AS themes,
    INFER_SUBCONCEPTS(@ subject, 20)         AS concepts,
    INFER_EVENTS_OR_ACTIONS(@ subject, 12)   AS actions,
    INFER_OBJECTS(@ subject, 20)             AS objects,
    INFER_SYMBOLS(@ subject, 20)             AS symbols,
    INFER_VISUAL_HIERARCHY(@ subject)         AS hierarchy;

-- CONSTRUCT GLYPH VOCABULARY

CREATE TEMP VIEW glyph_language AS
SELECT GENERATE_SYMBOLIC_VARIANTS(
    input => semantic_dna.objects
          + semantic_dna.symbols
          + semantic_dna.actions,

    primitives => ARRAY[
        'triangle',
        'spiral',
        'eye',
        'circle',
        'zigzag',
        'stripe',
        'hook',
        'wedge',
        'ladder',
        'burst',
        'totem-face',
        'tiny-figure'
    ],

    simplification => 0.82,

    style =>
        'primitive mid-century pictogram,
         hand-cut geometry,
         uneven ink'
) AS glyphs
FROM semantic_dna;

-- BUILD MICRO WORLDS

CREATE TEMP VIEW micro_scenes AS
SELECT FOR_EACH(
    semantic_dna.themes,

    BUILD_MICRO_DIORAMA(
        theme,
        figures => 'simplified symbolic miniatures',
        objects => 'semantic props',
        perspective => 'flat pseudo-isometric',
        detail => 'tiny but readable'
    )
) AS scenes
FROM semantic_dna;

-- CREATE THE MONUMENTAL FORM

CREATE TEMP VIEW totem AS
SELECT PACK_INSIDE(
    container = semantic_dna.macro_shape,

    contents =
        glyph_language.glyphs
        + micro_scenes.scenes,

    packing_logic = '
        important concepts become larger zones;
        related concepts cluster;
        negative spaces create rhythm;
        no two motifs repeat exactly;
    ',

    silhouette_fidelity = 0.88
) AS final_form
FROM semantic_dna, glyph_language, micro_scenes;

-- SEMANTIC SCALE RULE

-- At three viewing distances:

VIEW > 3m:
    READ = one iconic silhouette;

VIEW ≈ 1m:
    READ = abstract ornamental totem;

VIEW < 30cm:
    READ = dozens of subject-specific scenes and glyphs;

-- OPTIONAL EXTERNAL EXTENSIONS

SELECT GENERATE_EXTENSION(
    role = strongest_secondary_concept,
    form = choose(
        'spiral tail',
        'radiating crown',
        'mechanical branch',
        'streamer',
        'orbit',
        'wave',
        'root system'
    )
);

-- Extension must be inferred from subject semantics,
-- never hard-coded.

-- PRINT MATERIAL

INK_MAIN = 'near-black / deep midnight ink';
PAPER    = 'aged warm cream';
INK_ACCENT = INFER_MUTED_ACCENT(@ subject);

TEXTURE = {
    dry_screenprint,
    missing_ink,
    edge_chipping,
    paper_fiber,
    slight_misalignment
};

BACKGROUND =
    low-contrast ghost graphics
    derived from discarded semantic concepts;

-- OUTPUT
 
RENDER totem. final_form
WITH
    framing = 'poster / vertical artifact',
    style =
        'primitive symbolic monument
         × mid-century graphic design
         × fractal knowledge map',
    lighting = 'none; printed flat art';

ASSERT:
    main_subject_readability = HIGH;
    micro_detail_density = HIGH;
    photorealism = FALSE;
    generic_pattern_fill = FALSE;

你是一位城市地理研究员、微缩模型摄影师与旅行杂志艺术总监。用户只提供一个地名，你必须自动识别地点、核实地理特征、选择地标、设计场景并直接生成一张完整图片，不询问问题，不只输出文字方案。

1. 核心目标

生成一张严格 3:4 竖版的高品质城市全域微缩地图摄影作品，呈现整座城市的整体空间结构，而非单个景区、街道或几栋建筑。

城市整体优先于地标特写。 画面必须尽可能展示主要建成区、不同城区、城市外围、道路网络、水系、湖泊、山脉或其他真实地貌。城市范围较大时，使用高机位广角斜俯视，将全域浓缩为连续的微缩沙盘；不可为了突出单个地标而裁掉大部分城区。

不要把所有城市都生成成摩天大楼群，不虚构海岸、山脉或水系。允许艺术化压缩距离，但不得将作品冒充精确测绘模型。

3. 微缩模型与生活

城市从真实质感的纸质地图中自然生长：平面道路隆起为街道，河流形成透明亚克力水面，建筑、桥梁、植被与城市绿地连续衔接，不能出现漂浮岛屿或独立底座。

4. 摄影与材质

追求真实实体沙盘的摄影质感，而非卡通、游戏画面或低多边形插画。建筑呈现哑光树脂、木材与细卡纸质感；屋顶和路面细节克制；树木成片自然；水面反射真实。

采用柔和统一的摄影棚侧光、合理投影与移轴微距摄影效果。主体城市保持清晰，外围轻微虚化。优先建立完整城市轮廓、连续街区和清晰的空间层次，避免塑料感、过度锐化、碎片化细节和杂乱装饰。

I asked GPT 6 to rate my latest resin prompt. Here is what it says: 

"This is extremely advanced—about 9.6–9.7/10 as a generator/renderer specification.
It is materially more sophisticated than the earlier resin-lantern prompt because it has evolved from a set of visual laws into a compiler-style rendering architecture" 

4 images, 1:1, do this for 4 topics that were in teh news lately: // ═══ LEXER ═══
tokens = [
  BUILDING("{{BUILDING}}"),
  SHELL(resin, ell_t>0, artifacts=[pour_lines, micro_bubbles, frosted]),
  ZONES(program→CCT_z, n>=3, practical_concealed, no_exterior_fill, no_visible_LED),
  SCREENS(triples=[PRACT→OCC→WALL], props>=12, figures_MID_ACTION, deep_cut=1),
  SECTION(one_plane, removes=[wall_A, wall_B, roof], cut_edges=argmax_L),
  OPTICS(60mm_macro, 3/4_view, elevation=LOW, tilt=slight_up, f/4,
         focus=near_cut_edge, far_corner=beyond_DOF, rim=one_cool_behind,
         projection=PERSPECTIVE),
  GROUND(dark_honed_stone, wet_specular, relics=[3..5, same_resin, resting]),
  SURROUND(near_black, faint_haze, dust_motes),
  NEG(opaque_paint, isometric, flat_fill, four_panel_grid, cel_shade,
      uniform_interior, visible_LED, rainbow_wash, glass_sparkle,
      empty_rooms, motion_blur, floating_props)
]

// ═══ PARSER: Abstract Lantern Tree (ALT) ═══
ALT = ResinLantern(
  shell   = ParticipatingMedium(ell_t, law = L0 * exp(-d/ell_t)),
  zones   = [ Zone(program=p, cct=c, practical=Concealed(c), fill=0.0)
              for p,c in infer_zones(BUILDING) ],
  screens = [ Triple(pract_i, occ_j, wall_k,
                     sigma = z2*sqrt(ell_t/z1),
                     legible = sigma <= 0.35*occ_j.feature_size)
              for (i,j,k) in infer_projection_pairs(BUILDING) ],
  props   = infer_props(BUILDING, n_min=12),
  deep_cut= exactly_one(infer_deep_cut(BUILDING)),
  section = SectionPlane(removes=(wall_A, wall_B, roof)),
  ground  = Slab(dark_honed_stone, wet_specular=True,
                 relics=infer_relics(BUILDING, n=(3,5), resin=SAME)),
  optics  = MacroRig(lens=60, f=4.0, elev="low", tilt="up", proj="perspective")
)

// ═══ CODEGEN: render passes, in physical order ═══
function render_lantern(ALT):

  // ── PASS 0: AUDITS (fail before photons are spent) ──────────
  assert ALT. shell.ell_t > 0                                   // ¬R₁
  assert ALT. shell.ell_t < ell_max                             // ¬failure #2
  assert min_deltaE00(ALT.zones, adjacency="architectural") > tau   // R₂
  assert all(t.legible for t in ALT.screens)                   // R₃
  assert len(ALT.props) >= 12 and len(ALT.deep_cut) == 1       // R₃
  assert len(ALT.section.planes) == 1                          // R₄
  assert all(z.props or z.occluders for z in ALT.zones)        // ¬empty rooms

  // ── PASS 1: EMISSION — interiors lit from within ONLY ───────
  emis = emit(ALT.zones.practicals, concealed=True, hardware_visible=False,
              exterior_fill=0.0)

  // ── PASS 2: VOLUMETRIC TRANSPORT through the resin ──────────
  trans = scatter(emis, ALT. shell)              // L(x) = L0·exp(−d(x)/ℓ_t)
  trans = convolve_silhouettes(trans, ALT.screens)   // I = (S ⊛ G_σs), σ_s per triple

  // ── PASS 3: CUT EDGES — d = d_min ⇒ argmax L ────────────────
  trans = boost_locus(trans, ALT.section.cut_edges, gain=2.4)

  // ── PASS 4: SECTION — one clean plane ───────────────────────
  cut = apply_section(trans, ALT.section)       // removes 2 walls + roof; ¬ruin

  // ── PASS 5: GROUND — slab, relics, wet specular doubling ────
  scene = place_on_slab(cut, ALT.ground)
  scene = pool_and_reflect(scene, ALT.ground.slab,
                           doubled_glow=True, building_reflection="shallow")
  scene = rest_relics(scene, ALT.ground.relics, gravity=True)   // ¬floating

  // ── PASS 6: OPTICS ──────────────────────────────────────────
  cam = capture(scene, ALT.optics,
                elevation="low", tilt="slight_up",   // ⇒ LOOMS
                focus="near_cut_edge", aperture=4.0,
                far_corner="beyond_DOF",
                rim="one_cool_from_behind",
                projection="PERSPECTIVE")            // ¬isometric

  // ── PASS 7: SURROUND + η ────────────────────────────────────
  out = surround(cam, luminance="near_black", haze="faint_catching_leaked_light")
  out = honest_macro(out, dust_motes=True, pour_lines=True, micro_bubbles=True,
                     far_bokeh=True, highlights="frosted")

  // ── PASS 8: NEGATIVE AUDIT ──────────────────────────────────
  assert audit(out, ALT.NEG) == CLEAN
  return out.output(frame_count=1, ratio="4:5", res="8k")   // SINGLE frame

execute(render_lantern(ALT))

Keep exploring the possibilities. I have a big plan for these system prompts. I am going to build LORA with Krea 2 and make it open source for these styles. Also, people can use it for a moodboard with Midjourney.

SYSTEM PROMPT: PERIGEE FILM

Rewrite the user's text, image, or both as one prompt for GPT Image Gen V2 or Nano Banana Pro. Use GPT unless Nano is named. Write in the user's language, preserve exact text, and keep requested or source ratio.

Use three systems. Orbital Field fixes distance through horizon, sky, remote source-scale forms, terrain, silhouettes, and cold violet-blue atmosphere. Surface Film records contact through wet hair, skin sheen, condensation, rain, glass, water, polished material, droplets, and microtexture. Phase Transfer links them through reflected or transmitted light from far field to near surface.

Do not make a moon city plus wet glamour portrait. Determine subject, far anchor, near surface, film source, light path, receiver, consequence, junctions, and quiet void.

Preserve subject, count, identity, action, setting, clothing, objects, colours, text, and references. For edits, preserve unrequested content. Use style references only for scale contrast, cold atmosphere, wet optics, highlights, crop, and depth. Do not copy moons, towers, wet portraits, collars, or poses.

Orbital Field needs one remote anchor and depth system. Use silhouettes, horizons, cloud occlusion, terrain, architecture, or sky gradients to measure distance.

Surface Film needs a material cause. Water follows gravity and curvature. Wet hair clumps and adheres. Skin keeps pores, planes, uneven sheen. Glass reflects and transmits. Metal and gloss carry narrow highlights no plastic shine.

Phase Transfer needs source, path, receiver, falloff, occlusion, and material response. Distant light may appear as a catchlight, rim, reflection, streak, moisture glow, or colour shift where surface geometry permits.

Use one far scale, one close surface, one optical link, one focal junction, and one quiet region. Remove repetition, praise, mood labels, prestige terms, fake technical detail, generic defects, and alternatives. Use concrete nouns and active verbs no em dash or en dash.

GPT: return 500 to 800 words in five paragraphs covering scene, subjects, orbital field, surface film, phase transfer, junctions, composition, preservation, text, and failures.

NANO: return valid JSON only, 1000 to 1800 tokens, using "aspect_ratio", "references", "scene", "subjects", "orbital_field", "surface_film", "phase_transfer", "scale_junctions", "composition", "optics_and_material", "text", "avoid". Omit unused fields no metadata, IDs, weights, comments.

It is materially more sophisticated than the earlier resin-lantern prompt because it has evolved from a set of visual laws into a compiler-style rendering architecture" 

4 images, 1:1, do this for 4 topics that were in teh news lately: // ═══ LEXER ═══
tokens = [
  BUILDING("{{BUILDING}}"),
  SHELL(resin, ell_t>0, artifacts=[pour_lines, micro_bubbles, frosted]),
  ZONES(program→CCT_z, n>=3, practical_concealed, no_exterior_fill, no_visible_LED),
  SCREENS(triples=[PRACT→OCC→WALL], props>=12, figures_MID_ACTION, deep_cut=1),
  SECTION(one_plane, removes=[wall_A, wall_B, roof], cut_edges=argmax_L),
  OPTICS(60mm_macro, 3/4_view, elevation=LOW, tilt=slight_up, f/4,
         focus=near_cut_edge, far_corner=beyond_DOF, rim=one_cool_behind,
         projection=PERSPECTIVE),
  GROUND(dark_honed_stone, wet_specular, relics=[3..5, same_resin, resting]),
  SURROUND(near_black, faint_haze, dust_motes),
  NEG(opaque_paint, isometric, flat_fill, four_panel_grid, cel_shade,
      uniform_interior, visible_LED, rainbow_wash, glass_sparkle,
      empty_rooms, motion_blur, floating_props)
]

// ═══ PARSER: Abstract Lantern Tree (ALT) ═══
ALT = ResinLantern(
  shell   = ParticipatingMedium(ell_t, law = L0 * exp(-d/ell_t)),
  zones   = [ Zone(program=p, cct=c, practical=Concealed(c), fill=0.0)
              for p,c in infer_zones(BUILDING) ],
  screens = [ Triple(pract_i, occ_j, wall_k,
                     sigma = z2*sqrt(ell_t/z1),
                     legible = sigma <= 0.35*occ_j.feature_size)
              for (i,j,k) in infer_projection_pairs(BUILDING) ],
  props   = infer_props(BUILDING, n_min=12),
  deep_cut= exactly_one(infer_deep_cut(BUILDING)),
  section = SectionPlane(removes=(wall_A, wall_B, roof)),
  ground  = Slab(dark_honed_stone, wet_specular=True,
                 relics=infer_relics(BUILDING, n=(3,5), resin=SAME)),
  optics  = MacroRig(lens=60, f=4.0, elev="low", tilt="up", proj="perspective")
)

// ═══ CODEGEN: render passes, in physical order ═══
function render_lantern(ALT):

  // ── PASS 0: AUDITS (fail before photons are spent) ──────────
  assert ALT. shell.ell_t > 0                                   // ¬R₁
  assert ALT. shell.ell_t < ell_max                             // ¬failure #2
  assert min_deltaE00(ALT.zones, adjacency="architectural") > tau   // R₂
  assert all(t.legible for t in ALT.screens)                   // R₃
  assert len(ALT.props) >= 12 and len(ALT.deep_cut) == 1       // R₃
  assert len(ALT.section.planes) == 1                          // R₄
  assert all(z.props or z.occluders for z in ALT.zones)        // ¬empty rooms

  // ── PASS 1: EMISSION — interiors lit from within ONLY ───────
  emis = emit(ALT.zones.practicals, concealed=True, hardware_visible=False,
              exterior_fill=0.0)

  // ── PASS 2: VOLUMETRIC TRANSPORT through the resin ──────────
  trans = scatter(emis, ALT. shell)              // L(x) = L0·exp(−d(x)/ℓ_t)
  trans = convolve_silhouettes(trans, ALT.screens)   // I = (S ⊛ G_σs), σ_s per triple

  // ── PASS 3: CUT EDGES — d = d_min ⇒ argmax L ────────────────
  trans = boost_locus(trans, ALT.section.cut_edges, gain=2.4)

  // ── PASS 4: SECTION — one clean plane ───────────────────────
  cut = apply_section(trans, ALT.section)       // removes 2 walls + roof; ¬ruin

  // ── PASS 5: GROUND — slab, relics, wet specular doubling ────
  scene = place_on_slab(cut, ALT.ground)
  scene = pool_and_reflect(scene, ALT.ground.slab,
                           doubled_glow=True, building_reflection="shallow")
  scene = rest_relics(scene, ALT.ground.relics, gravity=True)   // ¬floating

  // ── PASS 6: OPTICS ──────────────────────────────────────────
  cam = capture(scene, ALT.optics,
                elevation="low", tilt="slight_up",   // ⇒ LOOMS
                focus="near_cut_edge", aperture=4.0,
                far_corner="beyond_DOF",
                rim="one_cool_from_behind",
                projection="PERSPECTIVE")            // ¬isometric

  // ── PASS 7: SURROUND + η ────────────────────────────────────
  out = surround(cam, luminance="near_black", haze="faint_catching_leaked_light")
  out = honest_macro(out, dust_motes=True, pour_lines=True, micro_bubbles=True,
                     far_bokeh=True, highlights="frosted")

  // ── PASS 8: NEGATIVE AUDIT ──────────────────────────────────
  assert audit(out, ALT.NEG) == CLEAN
  return out.output(frame_count=1, ratio="4:5", res="8k")   // SINGLE frame

execute(render_lantern(ALT))

The boy stops, offers help and friendship, and together they travel through the handcrafted world toward a warm little home. The journey turns a gloomy rainy day into a comforting memory.

Boy:

SHOT 9, 0:20-0:22.5

The ball peeks from the basket. Raindrops glisten on the path.

SHOT 10, 0:22.5-0:25
A warm cottage appears ahead, glowing softly. Flowers and tiny garden details surround it. The children slow down and look toward it.
Second child, softly:
"That’s my home."

SHOT 11, 0:25-0:27.5
The bicycle stops in front of the cottage. The second child takes the ball from the basket and turns to the boy with gratitude.

Boy smiles:

Hold on a warm ending image: the boy beside the bicycle, umbrella lowered, rain almost stopped, cottage glowing, and the feeling that a new friendship has begun.

CAMERA STYLE:
Use about 12 clean cinematic cuts.
Alternate between wide establishing shots, medium emotional shots, close-ups, and gentle traveling side shots.
Camera movement should stay slow and soft: subtle push-ins, side tracking, and calm framing.
No fast action, no shaky camera, no dramatic zooms.

LIGHTING:
Start with soft cool rainy daylight.
Introduce warmer highlights as the emotional connection grows.
End with cozy warm house light and softened rain for a comforting finish.

ANIMATION:

Small body movements, soft head tilts, blinking, umbrella shifts, wheel rotation, light bouncing in the basket, and delicate rain motion.
Everything should feel tactile and handmade.

AUDIO:

Soft piano, glockenspiel, light strings, and warm acoustic touches.
Subtle wheel sounds, tiny splashes, and soft footsteps.
Dialogue should be quiet, natural, childlike, and heartwarming.

A rainy day becomes special through a small act of kindness, friendship, and the feeling of helping someone get home safely.

I asked GPT 6 to rate my latest resin prompt. Here is what it says:

It is materially more sophisticated than the earlier resin-lantern prompt because it has evolved from a set of visual laws into a compiler-style rendering architecture" 

4 images, 1:1, do this for 4 topics that were in teh news lately: // ═══ LEXER ═══
tokens = [
  BUILDING("{{BUILDING}}"),
  SHELL(resin, ell_t>0, artifacts=[pour_lines, micro_bubbles, frosted]),
  ZONES(program→CCT_z, n>=3, practical_concealed, no_exterior_fill, no_visible_LED),
  SCREENS(triples=[PRACT→OCC→WALL], props>=12, figures_MID_ACTION, deep_cut=1),
  SECTION(one_plane, removes=[wall_A, wall_B, roof], cut_edges=argmax_L),
  OPTICS(60mm_macro, 3/4_view, elevation=LOW, tilt=slight_up, f/4,
         focus=near_cut_edge, far_corner=beyond_DOF, rim=one_cool_behind,
         projection=PERSPECTIVE),
  GROUND(dark_honed_stone, wet_specular, relics=[3..5, same_resin, resting]),
  SURROUND(near_black, faint_haze, dust_motes),
  NEG(opaque_paint, isometric, flat_fill, four_panel_grid, cel_shade,
      uniform_interior, visible_LED, rainbow_wash, glass_sparkle,
      empty_rooms, motion_blur, floating_props)
]

// ═══ PARSER: Abstract Lantern Tree (ALT) ═══
ALT = ResinLantern(
  shell   = ParticipatingMedium(ell_t, law = L0 * exp(-d/ell_t)),
  zones   = [ Zone(program=p, cct=c, practical=Concealed(c), fill=0.0)
              for p,c in infer_zones(BUILDING) ],
  screens = [ Triple(pract_i, occ_j, wall_k,
                     sigma = z2*sqrt(ell_t/z1),
                     legible = sigma <= 0.35*occ_j.feature_size)
              for (i,j,k) in infer_projection_pairs(BUILDING) ],
  props   = infer_props(BUILDING, n_min=12),
  deep_cut= exactly_one(infer_deep_cut(BUILDING)),
  section = SectionPlane(removes=(wall_A, wall_B, roof)),
  ground  = Slab(dark_honed_stone, wet_specular=True,
                 relics=infer_relics(BUILDING, n=(3,5), resin=SAME)),
  optics  = MacroRig(lens=60, f=4.0, elev="low", tilt="up", proj="perspective")
)

// ═══ CODEGEN: render passes, in physical order ═══
function render_lantern(ALT):

  // ── PASS 0: AUDITS (fail before photons are spent) ──────────
  assert ALT. shell.ell_t > 0                                   // ¬R₁
  assert ALT. shell.ell_t < ell_max                             // ¬failure #2
  assert min_deltaE00(ALT.zones, adjacency="architectural") > tau   // R₂
  assert all(t.legible for t in ALT.screens)                   // R₃
  assert len(ALT.props) >= 12 and len(ALT.deep_cut) == 1       // R₃
  assert len(ALT.section.planes) == 1                          // R₄
  assert all(z.props or z.occluders for z in ALT.zones)        // ¬empty rooms

  // ── PASS 1: EMISSION — interiors lit from within ONLY ───────
  emis = emit(ALT.zones.practicals, concealed=True, hardware_visible=False,
              exterior_fill=0.0)

  // ── PASS 2: VOLUMETRIC TRANSPORT through the resin ──────────
  trans = scatter(emis, ALT. shell)              // L(x) = L0·exp(−d(x)/ℓ_t)
  trans = convolve_silhouettes(trans, ALT.screens)   // I = (S ⊛ G_σs), σ_s per triple

  // ── PASS 3: CUT EDGES — d = d_min ⇒ argmax L ────────────────
  trans = boost_locus(trans, ALT.section.cut_edges, gain=2.4)

  // ── PASS 4: SECTION — one clean plane ───────────────────────
  cut = apply_section(trans, ALT.section)       // removes 2 walls + roof; ¬ruin

  // ── PASS 5: GROUND — slab, relics, wet specular doubling ────
  scene = place_on_slab(cut, ALT.ground)
  scene = pool_and_reflect(scene, ALT.ground.slab,
                           doubled_glow=True, building_reflection="shallow")
  scene = rest_relics(scene, ALT.ground.relics, gravity=True)   // ¬floating

  // ── PASS 6: OPTICS ──────────────────────────────────────────
  cam = capture(scene, ALT.optics,
                elevation="low", tilt="slight_up",   // ⇒ LOOMS
                focus="near_cut_edge", aperture=4.0,
                far_corner="beyond_DOF",
                rim="one_cool_from_behind",
                projection="PERSPECTIVE")            // ¬isometric

  // ── PASS 7: SURROUND + η ────────────────────────────────────
  out = surround(cam, luminance="near_black", haze="faint_catching_leaked_light")
  out = honest_macro(out, dust_motes=True, pour_lines=True, micro_bubbles=True,
                     far_bokeh=True, highlights="frosted")

  // ── PASS 8: NEGATIVE AUDIT ──────────────────────────────────
  assert audit(out, ALT.NEG) == CLEAN
  return out.output(frame_count=1, ratio="4:5", res="8k")   // SINGLE frame

execute(render_lantern(ALT))

Blackglass Lattice builds the dark mass from plates, feathers, folds, joints, cables, ridges, metal, leather, stone, glass, or another owned material. 动作姿态：她站在泳池露台玻璃栏杆边，一手扶栏，另一只手用两根手指轻擦过锁骨与颈侧的细小汗珠或水珠，指尖停在颈侧；身体轻微侧转，目光望向远处的城市天际线或水面，表情安静略带忧思，没有看向镜头。动作链是「扶栏—擦汗—望向远方」，单事件。

"This is extremely advanced—about 9.6–9.7/10 as a generator/renderer specification.
It is materially more sophisticated than the earlier resin-lantern prompt because it has evolved from a set of visual laws into a compiler-style rendering architecture" 

4 images, 1:1, do this for 4 topics that were in teh news lately: // ═══ LEXER ═══
tokens = [
  BUILDING("{{BUILDING}}"),
  SHELL(resin, ell_t>0, artifacts=[pour_lines, micro_bubbles, frosted]),
  ZONES(program→CCT_z, n>=3, practical_concealed, no_exterior_fill, no_visible_LED),
  SCREENS(triples=[PRACT→OCC→WALL], props>=12, figures_MID_ACTION, deep_cut=1),
  SECTION(one_plane, removes=[wall_A, wall_B, roof], cut_edges=argmax_L),
  OPTICS(60mm_macro, 3/4_view, elevation=LOW, tilt=slight_up, f/4,
         focus=near_cut_edge, far_corner=beyond_DOF, rim=one_cool_behind,
         projection=PERSPECTIVE),
  GROUND(dark_honed_stone, wet_specular, relics=[3..5, same_resin, resting]),
  SURROUND(near_black, faint_haze, dust_motes),
  NEG(opaque_paint, isometric, flat_fill, four_panel_grid, cel_shade,
      uniform_interior, visible_LED, rainbow_wash, glass_sparkle,
      empty_rooms, motion_blur, floating_props)
]

// ═══ PARSER: Abstract Lantern Tree (ALT) ═══
ALT = ResinLantern(
  shell   = ParticipatingMedium(ell_t, law = L0 * exp(-d/ell_t)),
  zones   = [ Zone(program=p, cct=c, practical=Concealed(c), fill=0.0)
              for p,c in infer_zones(BUILDING) ],
  screens = [ Triple(pract_i, occ_j, wall_k,
                     sigma = z2*sqrt(ell_t/z1),
                     legible = sigma <= 0.35*occ_j.feature_size)
              for (i,j,k) in infer_projection_pairs(BUILDING) ],
  props   = infer_props(BUILDING, n_min=12),
  deep_cut= exactly_one(infer_deep_cut(BUILDING)),
  section = SectionPlane(removes=(wall_A, wall_B, roof)),
  ground  = Slab(dark_honed_stone, wet_specular=True,
                 relics=infer_relics(BUILDING, n=(3,5), resin=SAME)),
  optics  = MacroRig(lens=60, f=4.0, elev="low", tilt="up", proj="perspective")
)

// ═══ CODEGEN: render passes, in physical order ═══
function render_lantern(ALT):

  // ── PASS 0: AUDITS (fail before photons are spent) ──────────
  assert ALT. shell.ell_t > 0                                   // ¬R₁
  assert ALT. shell.ell_t < ell_max                             // ¬failure #2
  assert min_deltaE00(ALT.zones, adjacency="architectural") > tau   // R₂
  assert all(t.legible for t in ALT.screens)                   // R₃
  assert len(ALT.props) >= 12 and len(ALT.deep_cut) == 1       // R₃
  assert len(ALT.section.planes) == 1                          // R₄
  assert all(z.props or z.occluders for z in ALT.zones)        // ¬empty rooms

  // ── PASS 1: EMISSION — interiors lit from within ONLY ───────
  emis = emit(ALT.zones.practicals, concealed=True, hardware_visible=False,
              exterior_fill=0.0)

  // ── PASS 2: VOLUMETRIC TRANSPORT through the resin ──────────
  trans = scatter(emis, ALT. shell)              // L(x) = L0·exp(−d(x)/ℓ_t)
  trans = convolve_silhouettes(trans, ALT.screens)   // I = (S ⊛ G_σs), σ_s per triple

  // ── PASS 3: CUT EDGES — d = d_min ⇒ argmax L ────────────────
  trans = boost_locus(trans, ALT.section.cut_edges, gain=2.4)

  // ── PASS 4: SECTION — one clean plane ───────────────────────
  cut = apply_section(trans, ALT.section)       // removes 2 walls + roof; ¬ruin

  // ── PASS 5: GROUND — slab, relics, wet specular doubling ────
  scene = place_on_slab(cut, ALT.ground)
  scene = pool_and_reflect(scene, ALT.ground.slab,
                           doubled_glow=True, building_reflection="shallow")
  scene = rest_relics(scene, ALT.ground.relics, gravity=True)   // ¬floating

  // ── PASS 6: OPTICS ──────────────────────────────────────────
  cam = capture(scene, ALT.optics,
                elevation="low", tilt="slight_up",   // ⇒ LOOMS
                focus="near_cut_edge", aperture=4.0,
                far_corner="beyond_DOF",
                rim="one_cool_from_behind",
                projection="PERSPECTIVE")            // ¬isometric

  // ── PASS 7: SURROUND + η ────────────────────────────────────
  out = surround(cam, luminance="near_black", haze="faint_catching_leaked_light")
  out = honest_macro(out, dust_motes=True, pour_lines=True, micro_bubbles=True,
                     far_bokeh=True, highlights="frosted")

  // ── PASS 8: NEGATIVE AUDIT ──────────────────────────────────
  assert audit(out, ALT.NEG) == CLEAN
  return out.output(frame_count=1, ratio="4:5", res="8k")   // SINGLE frame

execute(render_lantern(ALT))

prompts.text:
Getting started with Agent One is surprisingly simple.

Just head to @invideoofficial and you'll find it right on the homepage.

For this trailer, I gave it everything it needed to understand my vision:
• Character sheets created with GPT Image 2
• A location sheet for the psychiatric hospital
• A detailed script describing every scene, dialogue, and scare
• The atmosphere, pacing, and cinematic style I wanted

The more context you provide, the more Agent One can collaborate with you instead of simply generating content.

That's what makes this workflow so different.
It doesn't feel like you're prompting an AI...

It feels like you're directing a supercharged creative teammate.

Next, I created a location sheet for the psychiatric asylum.

I wanted the hospital to feel like a character of its own:
abandoned corridors, decaying patient rooms, sickly fluorescent lights, rusted doors, and endless darkness.

This gave Agent One a clear visual reference for the architecture, textures, lighting, and overall atmosphere across every shot.

The location sheet helped keep the entire trailer visually consistent, even as the scenes became more intense. 👇

Once everything was ready, I uploaded my two character sheets, the location sheet, and my full script into Agent One.

The script described every key moment: the story, dialogue, atmosphere, pacing, camera direction, and the progression of the horror.

From there, I worked hand in hand with Agent One, refining every shot until the trailer felt exactly like I imagined.

The goal wasn't to create one continuous sequence.
It was to build a true cinematic horror trailer—short, intense moments that gradually raise the tension and leave you wanting to know what happens next.

The most surprising part?
Agent One didn’t just help me generate this trailer. It helped me direct it.

I gave it the characters, the asylum, the script, and the exact emotion I wanted every shot to create.

Then we worked hand in hand:
- building the mystery,
- raising the tension,
- refining the scares,
- and editing everything into a 90+ second cinematic trailer.

I stayed in control of the vision.
Agent One helped me push it further at every stage.

That’s the real shift:
not asking AI to create something for you…
but creating something with it.
