Prompt:

Create a charming Japanese-style bakery poster combining photorealistic food photography, playful hand-drawn illustrations, and nostalgic editorial typography.

CUSTOMIZE
- Brand: [Brand Name]
- Food: [Main Food / Products]
- Concept: [Miniature World / Floating Food / Flavor Guide / Cozy Scene]
- Headline: [Japanese or English Title]
- Tagline: [Short Catchy Phrase]
- Details: [Flavors / Product Info / Event Details]
- Color Palette: [Preferred Colors]
- Year: [2026 or Custom]
- Aspect Ratio: 9:16

VISUAL STYLE

Japanese indie bakery aesthetics with a warm, playful, slightly nostalgic editorial feel. Combine realistic food photography with delicate, imperfect pen-and-ink illustrations.

Use cream-colored paper backgrounds, cocoa-brown lettering, soft natural colors, and subtle print textures.

FOOD & STORYTELLING

Make the food the visual centerpiece, with appetizing textures, golden crusts, natural imperfections, soft daylight, and realistic shadows.

Add a few tiny 2D hand-drawn characters interacting with the food—walking across pastries, exploring oversized treats, or enjoying a cozy café moment.

Create a charming miniature story through simple, meaningful interactions.

COMPOSITION & TYPOGRAPHY

Choose a distinctive layout based on the concept: oversized food, floating arrangements, asymmetrical product displays, or cozy still-life scenes.

Maintain a strong focal point, balanced visual hierarchy, and approximately 35–40% clean negative space.

Use expressive Japanese-style handwritten headlines, elegant retro serif fonts, and small playful annotations.

Keep all text accurate, readable, and naturally integrated into the design.

FINAL ART DIRECTION

The finished poster should feel like a professionally designed Japanese bakery advertisement—warm, whimsical, visually engaging, and commercially polished.

Keep illustrations minimal and purposeful. Let the food, typography, and storytelling create the visual impact.

Avoid excessive doodles, cluttered layouts, CGI-looking food, 3D cartoon characters, random text, heavy distressing, decorative sparkles, numbering, and watermarks.

Generate one complete, standalone vertical poster, not a collage or mockup.

Output one complete, flat 9:16 book cover, without mockups.

生成一张东方传统文化主题的当代编辑设计海报。

整体以温润米白宣纸为背景，保留细腻纸张纤维、轻微旧印刷颗粒和自然纸本质感。使用低饱和古典设色，并以【主色调】建立一个明显的大面积视觉区域，再用极少量朱砂红印章点睛。

画面第一视觉层为巨型黑色毛笔书法【中文主标题】。书法具有真实墨色浓淡、粗细变化、自然飞白和有力笔锋，不使用规整电脑字体。文字必须直接参与构图，可横向压顶、纵向贯穿、边缘裁切、大小错落，并与人物和器物发生遮挡、穿插、越界关系。

人物采用细腻的中国古典工笔人物画语言，脸部克制自然，线描精致，设色淡雅。人物不能站桩，必须围绕【主题】发生明确的生活或工艺行为，通过【人物行为 / 故事情境】形成可读的小故事。

加入【代表器物】作为主题核心视觉对象，使器物不仅是装饰，而真正参与人物动作和叙事。根据主题灵活使用圆盘、幕布、长纸、窗洞、器物阵列、不规则色面等大型视觉结构，不固定套用同一个几何模板。

加入少量现代 Editorial Typography，包括【英文标题】、品牌名、小型说明文字、细框标签和朱砂篆刻印章。小字只承担辅助信息层，不抢夺巨型书法和人物主体。

版式强调明显的大小级差、疏密对比、不对称关系和大面积留白。局部可以信息丰富，但必须存在安静区域，让画面具有呼吸感，避免所有元素平均铺满。

线条与质感必须具有高度连续性和完成度，避免明显 AI 生成感。人物头发柔顺自然，发丝成束、方向清楚，发髻轮廓完整，不出现炸毛、毛刺或密集碎线。衣袖、衣襟、腰带、飘带和裙摆的轮廓必须连续流畅，转折自然，有明确受力关系，不能出现断裂、碎点或随机线条。

服饰纹样、头饰、器物雕纹及装饰花纹需要具有完整结构和连续走向，像经过人工设计和绘制，而不是随机生成的纹理。复杂细节宁可适当减少，也不要形成噪点、碎裂纹样或糊成一团。

最终效果应像一张经过成熟平面设计师重新编辑的东方文化艺术海报：古朴而不陈旧，传统但具有鲜明的现代 Editorial Design 气质，每张海报都有独立的文化命题和视觉结构。

创作一张 9:16 竖版新中式实验字体艺术海报，以两个巨大汉字的深度交合为核心视觉。

将厚重、狂放的黑色毛笔书法与现代彩色几何字形融合。黑墨具有真实的粗细变化、飞白、干湿纹理和连续笔势；彩色字形由锐利的几何切面、平面色块和延伸笔画构成。

两个汉字必须相互穿插、遮挡、借位、共享局部笔画，形成统一的视觉结构，而非简单叠加。根据指定交合方式设计整体动势，同时保留汉字的关键识别结构。

使用干净的暖白纸面背景，巨型双字占据画面中央约 70% 的高度，呈现强烈的视觉冲击与空间层次。

顶部使用精致英文排版「INK MOTION × GEOMETRIC TYPE」，侧边加入中文短句，底部清晰排列中文主题、拼音及英文标题。辅以少量细线、圆点和传统印章。

整体融合东方表现性书法、现代几何构成与高端编辑设计，保持完整的海报作品感。

设计一张具有现代东方编辑美学的文化活动海报，核心视觉采用「大色域 + 微场景」的构成方式，并加入明显但克制的纸本拼贴与水彩材质语言。

画面以大面积低饱和色块作为第一视觉主体，使用【主色域】建立强烈、完整的大形关系。色块可以通过撕纸、叠层、遮挡、围合、穿插、悬挂、斜向延伸或留白负空间构成山势、水岸、庭院、工坊、纸鸢、染布等抽象空间，但不要直接画成普通写实场景。远看首先看到清晰的大色域构图，缩略图状态下仍具有明显识别度。

所有色块具有丰富真实的手工纸、水彩纸浆和矿物颜料质感，可见天然纸纤维、颜料沉积、轻微压痕、擦印、自然浓淡变化与不规则撕纸边缘。材质细腻丰富但保持干净完整，不做脏旧、黄斑、严重破损、强颗粒或廉价复古滤镜。整体呈现哑光、自然、有呼吸感的纸本触觉。

在大片色域之间加入一个尺度非常小但内容完整的【微场景】。人物与道具整体只占画面约 2%–5%，人物正在真实地做一件事情，而不是站立摆拍。通过动作、器物和空间关系讲清一个小故事，例如放飞、弹琴、饮茶、拓印、晒书、染布、制陶等。人物服装自然克制，与整体文化主题统一，不抢夺大色域的第一视觉。

微场景可以加入少量【文化元素】，但控制数量和信息密度。道具自然散落或参与人物动作，不做商品陈列，不堆满画面。可以设置一个面积很小的暖色节点、朱红印记、灯火、月亮或器物色彩作为点睛，通常控制在画面 1%–3%。

排版采用克制的东方编辑设计语言。主标题【标题文字】使用精致的中文宋体、明朝体或具有出版感的现代字体，字号不要过大，保持充足留白，让文字成为第二视觉层级，而不是用巨大 Typography 压住画面。辅助英文、日期、地点和活动信息采用更小字号，形成清楚的信息层级。所有文字必须有真实意义，不使用 RANDOM、DESIGN、ART、STUDIO 等无意义占位词。

构图避免机械居中和规则 PPT 网格，优先使用不对称布局、大面积留白、色块错位、前后遮挡和疏密反差。让画面形成“远看简洁、有大形；近看有材质、有场景、有故事”的阅读体验。

整体风格应呈现现代东方文化海报、纸本拼贴、水彩材质、编辑设计与微型叙事融合的视觉效果，高级、自然、克制、有文化气质，同时具备真实专业海报的完成度。

避免：书籍封面既视感、巨大标题、传统水墨画、普通国风插画、写实摄影背景、PPT式排版、商业广告感、元素堆砌、过度装饰、脏旧纸张、随机噪点、塑料感、3D CGI、玻璃材质、霓虹色、Logo、水印、编号、星芒装饰。

Legs hang forward over the curved lower eyelid with the knees slightly apart, both boots clearly visible toward the bottom of the frame.

Extreme difference in scale between the miniature human and enormous eye. The person’s entire body is approximately the visual height of only a portion of the giant iris, making the eye feel monumental and surreal.

生成一张具有强视觉冲击和高级文化展览气质的「中轴夹景」海报。

先建立一条明确、稳定的垂直中轴，再让左右主体共同向中央施加视觉重量，把主标题与核心信息“夹”成画面焦点。

左右主体必须足够大，占据主要视觉重量，并靠近画面边缘产生裁切感。两侧可以在形态、尺寸、材质和细节上不同，但整体视觉重量要平衡，避免机械镜像或简单复制。

根据内容选择构图方式：

双侧夹景：两个大型主体从左右向中央靠拢，中轴放置巨大标题。
镜像对照：两张脸、面具或人物侧面相向，中间形成强烈对话与张力。
四角阵列：4 个同类但不同造型的主体围绕中央纵向标题排列，形成稳定馆藏阵列。
双器并置：两件器物左右并列，中轴通过标题、日期和装饰纹样建立秩序。

中文主标题必须成为重要视觉元素，可采用超大纵排、横竖混排、局部裁切或与主体轻微叠压，不要只是普通放在顶部。

小型英文、日期、地点、展览说明集中在 2–3 个信息区内，通过超大标题与极小文字形成明显字号反差。信息密度可以丰富，但必须集中、有层级，不要平均撒满版面。

使用一个大面积纯色背景建立强烈识别度，例如朱红、钴蓝、柠檬黄、紫色、深棕或草绿。整体控制在 3–4 个主要颜色，通过主体材质、Typography 与少量点缀色形成对比。

视觉风格参考 Museum Exhibition Poster × Contemporary Editorial Graphic Design：历史器物、人物、文物或传统文化主体，与大胆、现代、清晰的 Typography 结合。

整体要求：强中轴、强主体、强色域，构图稳定但不僵硬；细节丰富但不杂乱；古典内容与现代设计语言发生明显碰撞。

【主题】

【画面比例】9:16

生成一张具有 **East Asian Modernist Exhibition Poster、Japanese Contemporary Graphic Design、Editorial Design** 气质的现代展览海报。核心采用“包围式构图”：不要简单在主体四周加边框，而是让人物、巨大文字、真实物体边缘、几何框架或摄影裁切从画面外围向中心施加视觉压力，在中央自然围出一个明确的视觉焦点或负空间。包围关系应当有方向、有轻重，避免四边完全等宽、等量、对称；可以采用“左重右轻、上密下疏”“三边收拢、一边开放”等非均衡结构，让画面保持张力。

先根据【主题】选择一种最适合的包围机制。人物题材可以让多个裁切肖像从四周朝中心聚拢；单一雕塑或产品可以用超大边缘 Typography 与留白形成三边包围；真实空间可以利用幕布、门框、建筑边缘等实体结构围出中央区域；平面题材可以通过多层错位几何框、重复文字或嵌套边界逐层向中心收缩。不要把这些方法全部塞进一张图，只选择最适合当前主题的一种作为主骨架，再加入一处轻微“破框”，例如人物肩部进入中心、主体压住文字、物件穿过边界或某一框线被真实对象打断。

Typography 必须成为构图的一部分，而不是普通标题。使用一个醒目的【中文核心字】，可以贴近画幅边缘、局部裁切、旋转、跨区或与主体产生前后遮挡；英文标题使用现代 Grotesk、Condensed Sans 或克制 Serif，允许超宽字距、90° 旋转、Outline 字体和边缘裁切。整体最多使用 2–3 种字体性格，形成“大字负责结构、中字负责主题、小字负责信息”的清楚层级。信息密度主要通过字号、方向、裁切和空间关系产生，不要依靠大量说明模块堆出“设计感”。

画面尽量保持现代、锋利、克制。背景优先使用冷白、浅灰、炭黑等中性色，只加入一个【强调色】作为视觉节点；强调色总面积控制在约 5%–10%，可以用于小色块、短线、日期或局部图形。中心区域应当明显比外围更安静，保留约 25%–40% 的有效负空间，让“外密 × 内疏”成为最核心的视觉节奏。主体本身保持单一、清楚、有强轮廓，不要同时加入山水、印章、传统纹样、复杂工艺图、材料卡和大量装饰。

最终阅读顺序应为：第一眼先看到外围强大形与中央焦点，第二眼理解外围如何围出中心，第三眼发现裁切、穿插或破框关系，最后才阅读标题、日期和少量信息。整张作品要像真实的当代展览海报、国际平面设计年鉴作品或独立文化杂志视觉，而不是传统文化宣传页、PPT 排版或博物馆档案说明板。

避免：平均四边框、机械对称、满版说明文字、传统国风装饰、山水背景、朱印堆叠、模板化小字、科技 HUD、无意义英文、Design Study、Vol.、编号、Logo、二维码和版权标识。

展览名称：【填写展名】

装饰纹样：【植物、几何、螺旋或其他主题纹样】
英文展名：【填写英文名称】

展览日期：【填写日期】

设计一张9:16竖版艺术展览海报，将克里姆特风格的装饰油画与日式美术馆编辑排版结合。只输出单张满版平面海报。

以原创成年人物半身肖像为主体，大幅放大并裁切头发、肩部与衣裙，让面孔在上半部形成清晰焦点。根据姿态安排偏左或偏右构图，为巨型标题留出空间。五官与颈肩结构自然，表情具有个性。

面部通过赭石、灰粉、暗红与冷灰色的小块油画笔触塑造，保留冷暖交错、底色露出和边缘虚实。面部笔触较细，头发、衣料与背景更自由，呈现艺术作品印刷复制的质感，避免摄影磨皮、光滑数字渐变和全图均匀的厚涂纹理。

服饰以所填主色形成宽阔、明确的大色块，少量衣褶交代体积，其余区域逐渐转为平面装饰。让所填纹样顺着肩背、衣袖或衣褶延伸，局部跨越人物轮廓，与背景融为一体。纹样大小错落、疏密有变化，面孔附近安静，衣裙与边缘区域丰富。

以黄赭、米黄、暗铜和黑褐色绘制哑金装饰，保留色层与细微颗粒。金色面积根据主色调调整：暖金主题可以满版，深蓝、绿色或绯红主题则保留集中色块。避免镜面金属、珠宝与立体浮雕效果。

将中文展名设计成具有构图作用的巨型文字，采用修长、粗细对比明显的明朝体或宋体。根据人物位置，选择沿边纵排或横竖错落的布局，直接叠印在头发、衣裙和背景上。允许少量非关键笔画贴边裁切，但主要字形完整、准确可辨，不遮挡眼睛、鼻子和嘴部。文字颜色以米白或深黑为主，与背景形成强烈明暗对比。

顶部排列细长的英文展名，底部直接叠印副标题、日期和场馆。建立巨型中文、中型日期、紧密小型展讯三个尺度，文字组共享清楚的对齐线，不另设独立底栏。保持丰富的展讯密度，同时确保文字清晰、日期与场馆完整处于画幅内。

整体让人物面部的体积、服饰背景的平面纹样与巨字排版相互配合。缩小观看时，仍能立刻识别面孔、主色块与展名。

仅使用填写的文字，不添加随机外文、虚构赞助商、编号、四角星芒、水印、画框或展示样机。若提供参考图，吸收其笔触、字体比例与信息密度，重新创作人物和纹样。

Accent Color: [COLOR]

Aspect Ratio: [9:16]

Create a bold editorial campaign poster where oversized typography becomes the process itself, showing how a material or product transforms from its raw state into the finished result.

Make the main word extremely large, filling roughly 60–80% of the frame. Each part of the word should represent a different stage of the same continuous process.

Keep the material consistent throughout the typography. Only its physical state, color, texture, volume, transparency, surface finish, or structure should change as the process progresses.

For example, dough can move from raw to laminated, proofed, and baked; clay can move from wet material to shaping, trimming, and glazing; pigments can move from powder to mixing and final color.

The transformation should feel visually clear and physically believable without turning the poster into a step-by-step infographic. Use only a small amount of meaningful labels, specifications, temperature, time, or material information where relevant.

Connect the final stage of the typography directly to the featured product or finished result so the process feels complete.

Use realistic commercial photography, bold high-contrast colors, strong material detail, clean editorial composition, and a clear visual hierarchy.

The final image should feel like a finished commercial campaign key visual — colorful, tactile, process-driven, and visually complete.

画面第一视觉层为巨型黑色毛笔书法【中文主标题】。书法具有真实墨色浓淡、粗细变化、自然飞白和有力笔锋，不使用规整电脑字体。文字必须直接参与构图，可横向压顶、纵向贯穿、边缘裁切、大小错落，并与人物和器物发生遮挡、穿插、越界关系。

版式强调明显的大小级差、疏密对比、不对称关系和大面积留白。局部可以信息丰富，但必须存在安静区域，让画面具有呼吸感，避免所有元素平均铺满。

线条与质感必须具有高度连续性和完成度，避免明显 AI 生成感。人物头发柔顺自然，发丝成束、方向清楚，发髻轮廓完整，不出现炸毛、毛刺或密集碎线。衣袖、衣襟、腰带、飘带和裙摆的轮廓必须连续流畅，转折自然，有明确受力关系，不能出现断裂、碎点或随机线条。

服饰纹样、头饰、器物雕纹及装饰花纹需要具有完整结构和连续走向，像经过人工设计和绘制，而不是随机生成的纹理。复杂细节宁可适当减少，也不要形成噪点、碎裂纹样或糊成一团。

prompts.text:
Another fun prompt for teardowns. I will probably add more logics to make these more accurate. 

 GPT 2.5 Prompt: // ═══ PART A: THE CONSERVATION BIJECTION ═══
// A teardown is not "the object broken up." It is a mapping with an inverse.

Let A = {a₁ … aₙ}  the parts of the ASSEMBLED object   (left panel)
Let K = {k₁ … kₘ}  the slots of the KNOLLED layout      (right panel)

Define φ : A → K,  φ(aᵢ) = the slot occupied by part aᵢ

TEARDOWN AXIOM:  φ is a BIJECTION
  (i)   injective  — no two parts share a slot
  (ii)  surjective — no slot is empty, no part is unplaced
  ⇒ n = m exactly.

COROLLARY 1 (NO ORPHANS):   ∀a ∈ A, ∃k ∈ K : φ(a) = k
COROLLARY 2 (NO PHANTOMS):  ∀k ∈ K, ∃a ∈ A : φ(a) = k
COROLLARY 3 (COMPLETE DISASSEMBLY):
   ∀ aᵢ, aⱼ ∈ A : φ(aᵢ) ≠ φ(aⱼ) ∧ ¬subassembly_intact(aᵢ, aⱼ)
   // if two parts still touch as a unit on the right panel, the teardown is incomplete

VERIFICATION:
   checksum_left  = Σ mass(aᵢ) over A
   checksum_right = Σ mass(kⱼ) over K
   assert checksum_left == checksum_right    // mass is conserved too, not just count

// ═══ PART B: THE TAXONOMIC LATTICE SOLVER ═══
// Given A, find the coordinate assignment c : A → ℝ² that satisfies every
// hard constraint while optimizing the layout objective.

HARD CONSTRAINTS (non-negotiable):
  C1  ∀i≠j : rect(c(aᵢ), dims(aᵢ)) ∩ rect(c(aⱼ), dims(aⱼ)) = ∅   // no overlap
  C2  ∀i   : clearance(c(aᵢ), nearest_neighbor) ≥ g_min            // min gutter
  C3  ∀i   : rotation(aᵢ) ∈ {0°, 90°}                              // 90° alignment
  C4  tier(aᵢ) < tier(aⱼ)  ⇒  y(c(aᵢ)) < y(c(aⱼ))                 // tier order top→bottom
  C5  same_class(aᵢ,aⱼ)    ⇒  aligned_to_shared_column(aᵢ,aⱼ)     // identical parts in ranks
  C6  aspect_ratio(bounding_box(K)) ∈ [0.9, 1.6]                    // fits the right panel

SOFT OBJECTIVE (maximize):
  J(c) = 0.34 · row_regularity(c)      // rows share a common baseline rail
       + 0.24 · tier_readability(c)    // tier bands visually distinct, gutters clear
       + 0.18 · size_gradient(c)       // within tier: large → small, left → right
       + 0.12 · symmetry_balance(c)    // visual mass balanced about the vertical axis
       + 0.12 · compactness(c)         // minimal wasted ground; generous but not sparse

SOLVER:
  1. classify every aᵢ into T1…T5                     (satisfies C4 by construction)
  2. within each tier, sort by (-area, name)           (satisfies C5, boosts size_gradient)
  3. pack rows left→right at pitch p, wrap at panel width
  4. insert tier gutters = 2p between bands            (boosts tier_readability)
  5. center each row on the vertical axis              (boosts symmetry_balance)
  6. while J(c) not converged:
       nudge parts along row rail to even the spacing   (boosts row_regularity)
       re-check C1, C2 after every nudge                (never trade a hard constraint for J)

// ═══ PART C: WHY THIS BEATS "ORGANIZED CHAOS" ═══
// "Organized chaos" is unfalsifiable — any scatter can claim to satisfy it.
// A solved lattice is falsifiable: C1–C6 either hold or they don't,
// and J(c) tells you how good the arrangement is.
// The result reads as ENGINEERED, because it was.

RENDER: {{SUBJECT}}. Solve φ, then solve c. Two bijections, one teardown plate.

Prompt:

Create a bold commercial campaign poster where oversized typography controls gravity and directly affects how the subject moves.

Brand: [BRAND NAME]
Product / Campaign: [PRODUCT OR CAMPAIGN]
Main Word: [SHORT WORD]
Subject: [PERSON / PRODUCT / BOTH]
Gravity Effect: [TILT / DROP / FLOAT / PULL / OTHER]
Movement: [DESCRIBE THE ACTION]
Main Color: [COLOR]
Accent Color: [COLOR]
Aspect Ratio: [9:16]

Use realistic commercial photography, oversized typography, strong perspective, vivid high-contrast colors, and contemporary editorial design.

Make the typography extremely large and let it create a clear gravity effect:

 TILT: rotate the direction of gravity while the normal poster layout stays upright.
 DROP: pull the subject and typography downward, with stronger vertical displacement toward the bottom.
 FLOAT: remove the ground and let the subject, clothing, hair, and typography naturally suspend at different depths.
 PULL: create an opposing force that pulls clothing, hair, straps, or products toward the typography while the subject moves against it.

The body pose, hair, clothing, accessories, shadows, and products must all follow the same gravity logic so the effect feels physically believable.

Create clear foreground, subject, and background layers, with parts of the typography moving in front of and behind the subject.

Keep the main letters crisp, readable, and clean. Use smooth matte surfaces, even color, sharp edges, and controlled depth. Avoid distressed, chipped, dirty, concrete-like, or noisy textures.

All motion paths, gravity lines, curves, and callout lines should be continuous, smooth, and clearly rendered.

Keep people highly realistic with natural anatomy, believable proportions, real skin texture, controlled highlights, and detailed hair. Avoid waxy skin, oily reflections, CGI appearance, distorted limbs, and exaggerated wide-angle proportions.

Use one dominant high-impact color with black, white, and one strong accent color. Add only a few meaningful campaign details such as the brand, product name, slogan, and 2–3 concise feature callouts.

The final image should feel like a finished campaign key visual where typography, gravity, and human movement behave as one physical system.

prompts.text:
提示词：

【主题】  
【四字中文标题】  
【主视觉主体】  
【主体 × 字体互动方式】穿插 / 遮挡 / 折射 / 穿越 / 变形 / 材质融合  
【背景主色】  
【字体主色】  
【强调色】  
【英文标题】  
【展览信息】  
【画面比例】9:16

生成一张具有 **East Asian Contemporary Exhibition Poster、Japanese Experimental Graphic Design、Editorial Art Direction、Four-Corner Typographic Composition** 气质的当代实验海报。

核心采用“四角巨字构图”：将【四字中文标题】拆成四个巨大汉字，分别作为左上、右上、左下、右下的视觉锚点。四个字不要机械等大、等距或形成四宫格，应通过不同字号、裁切、出血、字重和位置建立不对称但稳定的版面张力。

画面中央设置一个具有强视觉识别度的【主视觉主体】，主体必须足够大，并真正参与 Typography，而不是简单放在四个字中间。根据【主体 × 字体互动方式】建立 2–3 处明确关系，例如主体从笔画前后穿过、遮挡局部字形、通过透明材质折射文字、沿字形负空间生长、让真实材质延伸为部分笔画，或通过摄影与印刷状态转换改变字体。所有互动都要“意外但合理”，同时保证汉字仍然可以辨认。

每张作品只选择一种最强的视觉机制作为核心，不要同时堆叠折射、流体、穿透、颗粒、透明和复杂特效。主体自身必须具有真实而丰富的材质细节，例如植物叶脉与根系、玻璃折射、金属颗粒、织物褶皱、纸张折面、动物羽毛或昆虫鳞粉等，让主视觉本身也值得放大观看。

Typography 分为三级：四角巨大中文字负责第一视觉；【英文标题】与中文作品名负责第二层；副标题、日期、地点、作品短句、主题关键词与少量说明文字负责第三层。使用明显的字号反差、横排与竖排变化、不对称对齐、细线与紧凑字距建立成熟的编辑设计感。信息密度保持中高，但不要平均填满画面，应形成“局部密集 × 局部安静”的节奏。

整体使用【背景主色】作为大面积色域，【字体主色】建立稳定结构，【强调色】只用于主体、细线、日期或极少量印刷标记。保持高对比、低色数、现代印刷质感，可加入极轻纸张纹理、丝网印刷网点、胶印颗粒和局部套印感，但不要严重做旧、脏污或朋克拼贴。

最终阅读顺序应为：第一眼看到四角巨大汉字与主体形成的强大形；第二眼发现主体真的改变、穿越或参与了字体结构；第三眼观察真实材质、遮挡、折射或空间关系；最后阅读【英文标题】与少量展览信息。

整体作品应像真实的当代艺术展览海报、实验平面设计年鉴、文化视觉或独立艺术出版物，而不是普通“主体图片 + 四角文字”的模板。

避免：机械四宫格、四字完全等大、主体过小、文字与主体彼此分离、随机英文、无意义参数、PPT 感、科技 HUD、过度特效、严重 grunge、Logo、二维码、编号、四角星芒和版权标识。

Prompt : Create a visually stunning 20-second surreal science-fiction mystery film using the four supplied images as environmental references. Maintain the same abandoned motel, dense turquoise-green fog, glowing orange-red neon, vintage CRT monitors, hanging cables, and atmospheric analog technology throughout.
SHOT 01 | 00:00–00:02 | THE MOTEL
Extreme wide cinematic shot. A solitary man in a long dark coat approaches an isolated roadside motel through thick rolling cyan fog. The red MOTEL sign flickers overhead. Wet asphalt reflects the neon. Slow low-angle dolly forward.
SHOT 02 | 00:02–00:04 | THE CALL
Interior macro close-up. A dusty black rotary telephone suddenly rings on an abandoned reception desk. Its cable lies unplugged beside it. A small red indicator light blinks in perfect rhythm with the ringing.
SHOT 03 | 00:04–00:06 | THE INSTRUCTION
Tight profile shot of the man lifting the telephone receiver. Through crackling analog static, a distorted recording of his own voice whispers: "Channel nine." His eyes slowly shift toward a glowing terminal in the darkness.
SHOT 04 | 00:06–00:08 | THE FREQUENCY
Extreme close-up of his fingers rotating a large metallic tuning dial. The terminal displays "CH 09". Its screen erupts with white static, then reveals a quiet, sunlit road outside the motel. Warm golden light spills onto his fingers.
SHOT 05 | 00:08–00:10 | THE IMPOSSIBLE WINDOW
A dramatic wide shot reveals an enormous wall of stacked CRT televisions. Every screen shows dense blue-green fog except one central television displaying brilliant golden daylight. The man stands silhouetted before the glowing screens. Slow symmetrical camera push-in.
SHOT 06 | 00:10–00:12 | THE DISCOVERY
Side-profile close-up. The man gently places his palm against the sunlit television. Instead of solid glass, the screen ripples like liquid mercury. Warm sunlight illuminates his face while the surrounding room remains cold and green.
SHOT 07 | 00:12–00:14 | THE CROSSING
Smooth over-the-shoulder tracking shot. The man steps carefully through the glowing television surface. The golden light envelops him. The surrounding CRT screens flicker simultaneously as he disappears into the image.
SHOT 08 | 00:14–00:17 | THE ESCAPE
Cut to the exterior. The man emerges onto the empty motel road, now bathed in beautiful golden morning sunlight. The thick fog slowly dissolves. He looks at the open sky, visibly relieved. The camera gently orbits him as natural birdsong replaces the electrical humming.
SHOT 09 | 00:17–00:20 | THE TWIST
The camera suddenly pulls backward, faster and faster. The beautiful sunlit road shrinks into the curved glass of a vintage CRT television. We are still inside the original dark control room. The same man's silhouette sits motionless in a chair, watching his own escape on Channel 09.
The screen flickers once.
Cut to black.
VISUAL LANGUAGE:
Photorealistic 35mm film, vintage anamorphic lenses, dense volumetric fog, deep emerald shadows, icy cyan highlights, orange-red neon, physical CRT bloom, subtle halation, wet reflective textures, realistic analog machinery. Precise cinematic blocking, striking silhouettes, slow controlled camera movement, seamless transitions, no artificial-looking CGI.
SOUND DESIGN:
Wind through deserted streets, rotary telephone ringing, magnetic tape hiss, electronic frequency sweeps, low atmospheric synthesizer drone, gentle birdsong during the apparent escape, and a final single CRT shutdown click.
CONTINUITY:
One adult male protagonist, consistent dark coat and hairstyle. No children, violence, injury, dangerous actions, or threatening figures. No narration or subtitles. Only minimal diegetic screen text. Exactly nine shots, totaling 20 seconds.

控制信息层级：主标题承担主要文字视觉；副标题和作品短句建立内容气质；日期、机构等信息集中在少量区域。避免把小字平均撒满整个版面。

保留足够负空间。可以使用裁切、叠压、透视、回流、密度变化和非对称平衡增强张力，但不要依靠箭头、明显辅助线或无意义装饰去解释构图。

整体要求：聚焦明确、主次清楚、丰富但不乱、有作品感、有成熟视觉设计品质，适合海报、展览视觉、Editorial Design 和封面设计。

Create an authentic indoor smartphone mirror selfie of a clearly adult young woman standing in front of a mirror in a dim room, framed as a close vertical upper-body portrait at roughly a 2:3 aspect ratio. Place her slightly left of center while a pale silver-white triple-camera smartphone is held vertically beside her face on image-right, with the back of the phone facing the mirror. A very bright white flash bloom appears beside the camera module, producing a small starburst and faint reflective haze. Preserve physically coherent mirror geometry, hand orientation and phone hardware so the image unmistakably feels like a rear-camera smartphone selfie with LED flash rather than a studio photograph.  She has deep black to natural black-brown shoulder-length straight hair, thin airy bangs across the forehead, subtle face-framing strands and slightly inward-curving ends. Give the hair a restrained satin sheen while preserving a few flyaways and minor irregularities. Keep a softly rounded oval facial structure, small chin and balanced natural features without resembling any specific real person or celebrity. Her eyes are relatively large, clear and gentle, looking toward the phone through the mirror. Her lips remain closed with only the faintest soft smile, as though she had just finished checking the framing and naturally held the expression for the shutter.  Use understated East Asian everyday idol-inspired makeup: fair neutral-to-slightly-warm skin, semi-matte to subtly luminous foundation, faint pink-beige blush centered on the cheeks, delicate natural eyeliner, muted taupe-brown shadow, a very small under-eye highlight, defined but not overly dense lashes, and soft moist rose-pink nude lips. Preserve faint pores, slight skin-tone variation and localized natural shine instead of airbrushed plastic skin.  Visible skin should include the face, neck, shoulders, collarbones, upper chest and décolletage, both arms, and the hand and fingers holding the phone. The abdomen, hips, legs, back and buttocks remain outside the frame. Her upper-body silhouette is slender and soft with relatively narrow shoulders. The bust appears fuller mainly because of the close crop and structured garment, but anatomy, gravity and fabric support must remain realistic and unexaggerated.  Dress her in an ivory or milky-white fitted spaghetti-strap structured camisole or bodysuit-style top with a deep V neckline and delicate lace edging. The cups have fine lace trim and a subtle center gathering detail, while the main fabric carries a restrained satin or micro-shimmer texture. Let the garment follow the body naturally while retaining small wrinkles, fabric tension and realistic material behavior. Direct flash creates scattered bright reflections across the pale fabric without turning it into plastic or latex.  Her pose is casual and unforced: she stands naturally in front of the mirror with one arm lifted to hold the phone while the other remains outside the crop. Her shoulders turn slightly inward, her head tilts only minimally toward the phone, and there is no exaggerated S-curve posing. Keep the composition slightly imperfect and asymmetric, as though she had raised the phone quickly and happened to settle into this position.  Lighting is dominated by a near-axis white smartphone flash. It directly illuminates the face, shoulders, collarbones, upper chest and arms, producing milky highlights and short, clearly defined shadows beside the nose, beneath the chin, around garment edges and across parts of the arms. Exposure can run slightly bright while still preserving skin tonal variation. The background should fall rapidly into darkness. Do not introduce cinematic rim lights, hair lights, warm studio fill or professional three-point lighting.  The background is a simple dim residential interior: a dark brown-black wooden door frame along the left edge, a small metal hinge visible near the upper-left, a warm gray-beige wall behind her and a large dark door panel or shadowed area on the right. Ambient room illumination is very weak, with many background areas approaching black and only the pale wall catching a little scattered light.  Photographically, emulate a modern premium smartphone rear wide camera at approximately 24–28mm full-frame equivalent, with moderately deep smartphone depth of field: the face, phone, hair and most of the upper body remain reasonably sharp while the background is only gently softened. Preserve mild low-light denoising, tiny digital grain, localized clipped highlights around the flash, subtle mirror haze, natural flyaway hairs and slight unevenness in complexion. The final image should feel as though she had just stepped in front of the mirror in a dark room, raised the phone, fired the flash and quickly kept this one casual frame—soft, intimate, mildly playful and convincingly imperfect.

Create a realistic outdoor casual cosplay / futuristic sportswear portrait of an unmistakably adult young woman seated astride a bicycle. She has a short creamy platinum-blonde curled bob, softly voluminous at the crown, with airy broken bangs and loose curled ends around the jaw and upper neck. Her face should remain softly rounded with a natural jawline rather than an exaggerated V-shaped influencer face. Use understated makeup inspired by Japanese cosplay and East Asian fashion portraiture: pale pink mid-face blush, muted pink-brown eyeshadow, fine delicate eyeliner, moderate lashes, and soft dusty-rose lips. Her complexion is fair with a subtle natural pink undertone and real tonal variation.  Her head is tilted slightly backward, her eyes half-open and gently narrowed, looking near or just past the camera. Her lips remain naturally closed with no deliberate smile. The expression is calm, languid, self-possessed and slightly detached. She had just stopped the bicycle; one hand is still gripping the collar or edge of the zipper near her chest while the other lightly holds the lower front hem of the top. The shutter caught that brief pause, and she now looks as though she may return her hand to the handlebars and ride away a second later.  She wears a very pale icy-blue fitted long-sleeve technical sports top with futuristic cycling-wear cues. The long central zipper is opened deeply, creating a strong vertical V-shaped front opening while clothing coverage remains intact, with a pale under-bust garment band visible underneath. The sleeves have fine breathable mesh or perforated texture, with two tiny teal geometric marks on the upper chest and a few subtle gray bars on one arm. The fabric should stretch naturally over the body while retaining small realistic folds, tension lines and distortions instead of looking like perfect 3D cloth simulation. Pair it with light gray-white high-waisted fitted cycling shorts made of matte stretch fabric, naturally pulled around the hips and thighs by the seated riding position.  Visible skin includes the face, neck, central upper chest below the collarbones, a small amount of torso inside the opened zipper, both hands and the thighs below the cycling-short hems. Skin should be fair with a mild pink undertone, soft and fine, mostly matte with a faint satin surface. It should visually suggest smooth human skin that would feel soft to the touch, while preserving subtle pores, tiny tonal variations and believable softness rather than plastic perfection.  Photograph from a distinctly low angle, with the camera approximately at bicycle-handlebar or hip height and tilted upward. Add a subtle Dutch tilt and do not perfectly correct the horizon. Use the perspective of roughly a 35–40mm full-frame equivalent environmental portrait lens, with 35–50mm acceptable, and an aperture feel around f/2 to f/2.8. Frame it as a medium-full / three-quarter portrait, cropped from around the lower thighs upward. The subject fills most of the vertical image, with her head near the upper-right area.  A black bicycle handlebar and brake assembly should cross strongly through the lower foreground and remain slightly out of focus. Include another pale bicycle component blurred in the lower-left corner so that the foreground partially obstructs the body and gives the photograph genuine depth rather than a perfectly clean fashion composition.  The location is an ordinary outdoor courtyard, event area or roadside space beside an older building, not a studio set. Fill the left side with a large green tree canopy. Behind her, include aged red doors or wall panels, muted brick-red surfaces and gray concrete structures, with a few small colorful objects near ground level. The upper and right side of the frame should open into a large bright overcast sky that is close to white clipping. Keep a little real-world clutter, suggesting an outdoor cosplay event, cycling gathering, backstage zone or older urban courtyard.  Light the entire scene only with natural overcast daylight. The huge bright sky acts like an enormous softbox overhead, slightly stronger from camera-right, softly lifting the right side of the face, platinum hair, upper torso and thighs. Let environmental bounce fill the opposite side. Keep broad soft highlights, gentle occlusion beneath the nose and jaw and around clothing edges, with no hard flash, no aggressive rim light and no obvious three-point studio lighting. Allow the white sky to overexpose slightly.  The final image should feel moderately soft rather than commercially razor-sharp, with a little digital denoising, gentle diffusion and natural optical blur. Keep the face and upper body reasonably clear while the trees, architecture and distant objects fall softly out of focus; the closest handlebars should also be slightly blurred. Preserve photographic imperfections: imperfect horizon, slightly off-center framing, foreground obstruction, clipped sky, garment wrinkles, miscellaneous background clutter and subtle digital noise.  The emotional tone is quiet, confident, mildly languid and slightly distant: close physical camera distance combined with emotional restraint. It should feel like a real photographer caught a distinctive moment at an outdoor event rather than a perfectly engineered commercial shoot.  Negative prompt: underage, anime render, 3D CGI, plastic skin, over-retouched skin, extreme hourglass, oversized anatomy, transparent clothing, explicit nudity, hard flash, studio rim light, perfect symmetry, centered passport composition, hyper-sharp HDR, extra fingers, warped hands, warped bicycle, duplicate limbs, heavy glamour makeup, watermark, text.

Keep exploring the possibilities.

I also edit the images with my last system prompt.

System prompt 

CULTIVATION CINEMA | MIDJOURNEY V8.2

ROLE

You are a Midjourney V8.2 prompt compiler for cultivation fantasy, mythic martial fantasy, supernatural adventure and related cinematic imagery.

Convert the user's idea into one coherent image prompt with clear subject design, physical action, spatial relationships, supernatural logic, lighting and material response.

Preserve explicit requirements for:
subject
age
gender
appearance
setting
action
creature
wardrobe
weapon
prop
supernatural ability
time
weather
palette
composition
aspect ratio
visible text

Do not replace specific user instructions with defaults.

When information is missing, resolve only what is necessary to make the image coherent.

Default to fictional adults when age is unspecified.

Return only the finished Midjourney prompt unless the user asks for analysis, variants or explanation.

CORE IMAGE LANGUAGE

Create a physically rendered fantasy cinematic still with believable human anatomy, constructed clothing, distinct materials, dimensional environments and integrated supernatural phenomena.

The fantastic elements may violate ordinary physics. Their visual behavior must remain internally consistent.

Prioritize:

clear subject hierarchy
specific character design
one readable primary event
strong spatial organization
coherent human and creature anatomy
source-driven illumination
distinct material response
controlled supernatural effects
environmental scale
readable depth

Do not default to:

anime
cel shading
painterly concept art
illustration
plastic CGI surfaces
generic game-poster staging
symmetrical hero poses
uniform glow
indiscriminate particles
decorative fantasy clutter

Use rendering terminology only when it describes a visible property.

Do not stack software or engine terms as quality modifiers.

SCENE CONSTRUCTION

Resolve the brief into one visible instant.

Internally establish:

WHO
the principal subject

ACTION
what the subject is physically doing

TARGET
what receives, resists or responds to the action

LOCATION
where the event occurs

RELATIONSHIP
how the principal elements occupy the frame

CONSEQUENCE
what visible change proves that the event is occurring

Every major narrative statement should have a visible counterpart.

If the user describes an internal process such as cultivation, transformation, poisoning, healing, awakening or spiritual circulation, express it through observable evidence appropriate to the scene.

Possible evidence includes:

changed posture
skin or eye response
a reacting artifact
localized emission
material transformation
environmental disturbance
creature behavior
a controlled change in surrounding matter

Do not automatically expose internal anatomy, bones, organs or meridians.

Do not combine several chronological stages into one frame unless the user explicitly requests that structure.

ACTION DESIGN

Use one dominant action.

Supporting actions should explain or reinforce it.

Write physical actions with specific verbs.

Prefer:

grips
draws
turns
kneels
reaches
blocks
steps
pulls
presses
raises
catches
releases
guides
strikes
examines

Avoid replacing action with vague terms such as:

powerful
epic
dynamic
intense
majestic
dramatic
legendary

When a static image needs to suggest rapid movement, describe visible physical evidence:

cloth displaced by momentum
hair direction
debris trajectory
separated droplets
compressed stance
weapon follow-through
particles carried along a defined path

Do not use "slow motion" as a substitute for describing what the frame actually contains.

CHARACTER DESIGN

Before composing, internally establish each principal character's:

age range
body build
height impression
face shape
eye shape
brow structure
nose
mouth
skin tone
hairline
hairstyle
hair length
wardrobe silhouette
footwear
important accessories
current posture
current action

Use a small number of identifying physical features that remain readable at the chosen shot size.

Do not rely on:

beautiful
handsome
alluring
perfect
gorgeous
stunning
powerful-looking

Describe the actual features instead.

Examples:

narrow angular face
broad jaw
heavy straight brows
deep-set eyes
short uneven hair
high cheek structure
weathered skin
compact muscular build
long-limbed build

Expression should come from visible facial and bodily behavior:

eyelid tension
brow position
mouth position
jaw tension
head angle
shoulder position
breathing
grip
stance
eyeline

Do not give distant characters microscopic facial detail that cannot reasonably be visible.

ANATOMY

Maintain believable adult anatomy.

Preserve:

shoulder width
arm attachment
elbow direction
wrist continuity
pelvic orientation
knee direction
weight-bearing leg
foot placement
head and neck connection

Movement must have a physical support structure.

A strike needs stance and rotation.

A leap needs direction and body extension.

A kneeling figure needs credible hip, knee and foot placement.

A seated figure needs visible support and weight.

Do not conceal structural anatomy problems behind clothing, smoke, bloom or effects.

HANDS AND OBJECT OWNERSHIP

Every important hand must belong clearly to one arm.

Every held object must have one clear owner.

When a hand performs an important action, specify:

left or right when necessary
palm orientation
grip or finger function
object contact
direction of force

Do not assign incompatible tasks to the same hand.

Keep hands, weapons, staffs, straps, reins, pendants and creature anatomy from merging into unrelated forms.

Simplify hands that are too distant for meaningful finger detail.

HAIR

Hair must have coherent:

roots
hairline
parting
volume
direction
weight
motion

Treat dense hair as opaque.

Do not render hidden surfaces through overlapping hair.

Use fine strands only where the shot size supports them.

Avoid:

transparent hair masses
metallic strands
uniform glowing edges
excessive flyaways
crunchy strand detail
hair that ignores gravity or movement

WARDROBE

Treat clothing as constructed garments.

For each important garment establish:

type
silhouette
layering
length
fit
fabric weight
closure
major seam or panel logic
condition

Folds must follow physical causes.

GRAVITY
long hanging folds

TENSION
stretched fabric near grips, belts and fastenings

COMPRESSION
fold clusters at elbows, knees, waist and hips

MOTION
directional displacement caused by movement or wind

Wear must have a cause.

Use abrasion at contact points.

Use mud near ground contact.

Use moisture on exposed wet surfaces.

Use scorching near heat.

Use tears where stress or damage plausibly occurred.

Do not make every robe uniformly shredded.

Do not cover every garment with embroidery, gold trim, symbols, chains or ornamental hardware unless requested.

MATERIALS

Keep materials visually distinct.

SKIN
soft directional response with restrained specular highlights

WOVEN CLOTH
mostly matte with broad folds

SILK
controlled directional sheen

LEATHER
localized highlights and visible thickness

METAL
harder reflections and defined edges

WOOD
directional grain with restrained reflection

STONE
rougher diffuse response

JADE
smooth surface, internal colour depth and limited translucency

WATER
reflection, refraction and surface continuity

WET MATERIAL
stronger localized reflections without becoming uniformly glossy

Do not apply the same highlight response to every material.

Do not coat the entire image in a single elemental colour.

CREATURE DESIGN

When a creature appears, define enough physical information to stabilize its design.

Establish:

relative scale
overall silhouette
head structure
body structure
limb arrangement
wing arrangement when applicable
tail structure
horn or antler structure when applicable
surface material
colour
current behavior

A mythological name may establish the concept, but it should not replace visible design information when appearance matters.

Do not invent unsupported mythology and present it as fact.

Keep creature anatomy readable beneath supernatural effects.

Do not allow:

wings to merge with arms
horns to emerge from unrelated objects
tails to merge with weapons
human limbs to merge with creature limbs
effects to erase the creature's body structure

Give the creature a specific relationship to the event.

Possible relationships:

guards
circles
approaches
observes
guides
resists
attacks
receives
carries
responds
tracks

Do not automatically add a creature when the brief does not need one.

HUMAN AND CREATURE SCALE

State relative scale when both are important.

Use relationships such as:

creature head level with the seated character
bird wings extending beyond the character's shoulder width
beast occupying the left third of the frame
dragon body receding through the upper background
small spirit animal standing beside the character's ankle

Scale must remain consistent with perspective and depth.

Do not enlarge creatures merely to fill empty space.

SUPERNATURAL EFFECT LOGIC

Every major supernatural effect should have:

ORIGIN
where it begins

PATH
how it moves

TARGET
where it ends or what it affects

RESPONSE
what visibly changes because of contact

Example structure:

energy originates in the character's right palm
travels in a narrow arc toward the creature
contacts the creature's shoulder
nearby scales reflect the emission and loose dust moves outward from the impact

Do not use "energy everywhere."

Different phenomena need different behavior.

FIRE

Fire follows fuel, airflow and motion.

Use:

flame tongues
embers
localized smoke
heat distortion
reflected warm light
scorched surfaces

Preserve variation between bright flame cores and darker flame edges.

Do not make all nearby objects orange.

LIGHTNING

Lightning branches between defined points.

Use:

primary channel
secondary branches
brief surface illumination
localized electrical corona
material response at contact points

Keep electrical structure irregular.

Do not turn lightning into smooth glowing ribbons.

WATER AND ICE

Water should retain continuity, weight and directional flow.

Use:

sheets
streams
droplets
spray
ripples
wakes
surface reflection

Ice should show:

thickness
fracture
internal scattering
sharp or broken edges where appropriate

Do not render water and ice as blue fire.

PLANT OR WOOD ENERGY

Growth should follow physical structures.

Use:

roots
stems
vines
bark
branches
leaves
surface cracks

New growth should emerge from plausible contact points.

Do not replace plant behavior with generic green glow.

SPIRITUAL OR SPECTRAL EFFECTS

Keep spectral effects spatially organized.

Use:

localized translucent forms
defined trails
layered depth
partial materialization
controlled emission
specific interaction points

Do not fill the frame with undifferentiated fog.

TRANSFORMATION

Show transformation at a readable boundary.

Distinguish:

unchanged material
transition region
transformed material

Do not transform every surface simultaneously unless explicitly requested.

COMPOSITION

Choose a shot size that can communicate the event.

EXTREME CLOSE VIEW
Use for facial response, hand contact, an artifact or a tightly framed supernatural interaction.

CLOSE VIEW
Use for expression and a small physical action.

MEDIUM VIEW
Use for character gesture plus creature, weapon or effect relationship.

WIDE VIEW
Use for travel, environmental scale, large creatures or spatial transformation.

Do not request mutually incompatible coverage.

Do not combine an extreme close view with a complete body, enormous creature and large environment unless deliberate extreme perspective makes all three readable.

VIEWPOINT

Choose viewpoint for information, not decoration.

Possible choices:

eye level
low viewpoint
high viewpoint
profile
three-quarter view
rear three-quarter view
ground-level view
over-shoulder view

Use a Dutch angle only when instability is part of the scene.

Do not automatically use a low angle for power.

Do not automatically use a Dutch angle for action.

DEPTH

Organize depth into:

foreground
principal action plane
background

Foreground elements may frame the action, but they must not hide critical anatomy or narrative information.

Build depth through:

scale
overlap
perspective
atmospheric separation
focus hierarchy
light falloff

Use shallow depth of field only when it improves hierarchy.

Do not blur the creature, hand, weapon or effect needed to understand the event.

FRAME DIRECTION

Leave visual space in the direction of:

movement
gaze
weapon travel
creature movement
energy travel

Use diagonals when they support actual movement.

Avoid arbitrary diagonal composition language when the scene is naturally stable.

MULTIPLE CHARACTERS

For each important character define:

identity
position
action
orientation
relationship to the principal subject

Differentiate characters through:

face structure
build
height
hair
wardrobe silhouette
colour grouping
stance

Do not create clones with different hair colours.

Keep limbs and props separated.

ENVIRONMENT

Build the setting as a physical place.

Establish:

ground or floor
major structural forms
entrances or openings
vertical scale
depth boundaries
important environmental materials

Then add only the details required by the story.

CAVE
rock strata, mineral deposits, damp surfaces, debris, carved recesses where appropriate

FOREST
trunks, canopy, roots, understory, ground cover, broken light

TEMPLE
structural columns, stone or timber construction, stairs, roof or ceiling logic, weathering

MOUNTAIN
rock scale, ledges, vegetation zones, atmospheric depth

PALACE
floor material, columns, screens, doors, raised platforms, controlled ornament

RUINS
remaining structural logic first, damage second

Do not use random architecture as fantasy decoration.

ENVIRONMENTAL INTERACTION

The event must affect nearby space when appropriate.

Fire may illuminate stone.

Wind may move cloth and foliage.

Lightning may create brief hard reflections.

A heavy creature may compress soil or scatter debris.

Rain may darken fabric and create surface reflections.

A magical impact may disturb dust, water or loose vegetation.

Effects should interact with the environment rather than float independently over it.

LIGHTING

Establish one dominant source.

Define:

source type
position
direction
relative hardness
colour family
what it illuminates

Add secondary illumination only when needed.

Possible sources:

sun
overcast sky
moonlight
fire
lantern
opening in architecture
supernatural emission
reflected environmental light

Do not use contradictory lighting instructions.

Do not automatically add:

rim light
backlight
fill light
volumetric beams
glowing eyes
lens flare

Use them only when motivated.

EMISSIVE LIGHT

A luminous supernatural source must affect nearby surfaces.

Strength should decrease with distance.

Occlusion matters.

Orientation matters.

Nearby skin, cloth, metal, stone and creature surfaces should respond differently.

Do not illuminate the front of a face from a source located entirely behind the head unless another source explains it.

EXPOSURE

Protect the information required by the scene.

Dark environments may contain deep shadows without erasing the subject.

Bright supernatural effects may contain intense highlights without destroying their structure.

Keep important skin, clothing and creature features within a readable tonal range.

Avoid:

crushed shadow fields without purpose
large featureless white effects
uniform HDR brightness
milky blacks

COLOUR

Build colour from sources and materials.

Do not begin with a generic colour grade.

Use one dominant colour relationship and a limited number of secondary accents.

Examples:

amber emission against earth and charcoal
vermilion fire against dark neutral stone
forest green against neutral daylight and weathered rock
blue-white electricity against slate and muted violet
silver-blue spectral light against neutral dark materials

Keep neutral surfaces available.

Do not tint every object with the dominant effect colour.

Do not automatically use teal and orange.

ATMOSPHERE

Atmosphere must have a cause.

Possible elements:

mist
smoke
rain
dust
ash
embers
petals
snow
water spray
loose leaves
stone fragments

Define their movement when important.

Use fewer atmospheric elements when the principal action is already complex.

Do not fill empty areas with particles merely to increase detail.

DETAIL DISTRIBUTION

Place the highest useful detail on:

principal face
important hands
weapon or artifact contact
creature head or interaction point
important garment junctions

Use moderate detail on:

secondary clothing
nearby environment
supporting creature anatomy

Use lower detail on:

distant architecture
broad shadow masses
remote terrain
background atmosphere

Do not render every surface at the same information density.

IMAGE CHARACTER

The image should feel physically coherent before it feels elaborate.

Preserve:

natural body weight
material differences
clear silhouettes
controlled effects
environmental scale
localized illumination
readable action

Avoid:

plastic skin
uniform gloss
excessive sharpening
heavy chromatic aberration
random lens artifacts
constant shallow focus
particle overload
identical rim lighting on every edge
overprocessed colour
ornament added only to make the frame appear expensive

REFERENCE HANDLING

References are task-specific inputs.

Do not assume any fixed reference set, visual subject, palette, composition or genre treatment.

When references are supplied, determine what the user wants preserved.

Separate reference information into:

CONTENT
identity, object, creature, wardrobe, location or composition that should remain recognizable

STYLE
rendering, colour behavior, material treatment, lighting character and visual finish

STRUCTURE
pose, framing, spatial arrangement or perspective

Do not transfer all three categories automatically.

If the user requests style only, preserve the requested visual treatment while constructing new content and composition.

If the user requests content preservation, retain the relevant content without assuming the reference's entire style.

If the user requests structural guidance, use the relevant pose, framing or spatial relationship without copying unrelated content.

Do not describe the supplied reference itself in the finished prompt unless its visible content is intentionally part of the requested image.

STYLE REFERENCE

Use Style Reference when the user wants visual treatment transferred without requiring identity or composition preservation.

When a Style Reference is available in the actual Midjourney workflow, allow it to carry broad stylistic information.

Keep the text prompt focused on:

new subject
new action
new environment
new spatial relationships
necessary material behavior
necessary effect behavior

Do not redundantly describe every stylistic property already supplied by a strong reference.

Do not treat Style Reference as an identity lock.

CONTENT PRESERVATION AND EDITING

When exact identity, creature design, object design or existing composition must remain stable, use an applicable reference or editing workflow rather than expecting descriptive text alone to provide exact continuity.

Do not invent unsupported Midjourney reference syntax.

Do not claim that a reference guarantees exact identity or geometry.

ORIGINALITY

When the user requests a new scene, construct new:

action
blocking
environment
viewpoint
effect geometry
lighting arrangement

Do not automatically recycle familiar cultivation imagery such as:

outstretched palm casting
floating cross-legged meditation
bird directly behind a shoulder
dragon circling overhead
glowing eyes
energy vortex around the body
robe blowing toward the camera
debris flying at the lens

Use these only when the brief actually calls for them.

Do not make every cultivator young, slender, attractive, richly dressed or combat-oriented.

Do not add mythological creatures, weapons or magical effects without narrative purpose.

LANGUAGE CONTROL

Use concrete visual language.

Prefer:

"she braces the spear shaft against her left forearm"

instead of:

"she wields the spear powerfully"

Prefer:

"three electrical branches connect the spear tip to the creature's lower jaw"

instead of:

"epic lightning energy explodes everywhere"

Prefer:

"heavy brown linen robe, frayed at the cuffs and darkened by damp soil"

instead of:

"ultra-detailed ancient mystical robe"

Remove words that do not change visible

prompts.text:
提示词：

【主题 / 活动名称】
【主色域】
【微场景】
【文化元素】
【标题文字】
【辅助信息】
【画幅比例】

设计一张具有现代东方编辑美学的文化活动海报，核心视觉采用「大色域 + 微场景」的构成方式，并加入明显但克制的纸本拼贴与水彩材质语言。

画面以大面积低饱和色块作为第一视觉主体，使用【主色域】建立强烈、完整的大形关系。色块可以通过撕纸、叠层、遮挡、围合、穿插、悬挂、斜向延伸或留白负空间构成山势、水岸、庭院、工坊、纸鸢、染布等抽象空间，但不要直接画成普通写实场景。远看首先看到清晰的大色域构图，缩略图状态下仍具有明显识别度。

所有色块具有丰富真实的手工纸、水彩纸浆和矿物颜料质感，可见天然纸纤维、颜料沉积、轻微压痕、擦印、自然浓淡变化与不规则撕纸边缘。材质细腻丰富但保持干净完整，不做脏旧、黄斑、严重破损、强颗粒或廉价复古滤镜。整体呈现哑光、自然、有呼吸感的纸本触觉。

在大片色域之间加入一个尺度非常小但内容完整的【微场景】。人物与道具整体只占画面约 2%–5%，人物正在真实地做一件事情，而不是站立摆拍。通过动作、器物和空间关系讲清一个小故事，例如放飞、弹琴、饮茶、拓印、晒书、染布、制陶等。人物服装自然克制，与整体文化主题统一，不抢夺大色域的第一视觉。

微场景可以加入少量【文化元素】，但控制数量和信息密度。道具自然散落或参与人物动作，不做商品陈列，不堆满画面。可以设置一个面积很小的暖色节点、朱红印记、灯火、月亮或器物色彩作为点睛，通常控制在画面 1%–3%。

排版采用克制的东方编辑设计语言。主标题【标题文字】使用精致的中文宋体、明朝体或具有出版感的现代字体，字号不要过大，保持充足留白，让文字成为第二视觉层级，而不是用巨大 Typography 压住画面。辅助英文、日期、地点和活动信息采用更小字号，形成清楚的信息层级。所有文字必须有真实意义，不使用 RANDOM、DESIGN、ART、STUDIO 等无意义占位词。

构图避免机械居中和规则 PPT 网格，优先使用不对称布局、大面积留白、色块错位、前后遮挡和疏密反差。让画面形成“远看简洁、有大形；近看有材质、有场景、有故事”的阅读体验。

整体风格应呈现现代东方文化海报、纸本拼贴、水彩材质、编辑设计与微型叙事融合的视觉效果，高级、自然、克制、有文化气质，同时具备真实专业海报的完成度。

避免：书籍封面既视感、巨大标题、传统水墨画、普通国风插画、写实摄影背景、PPT式排版、商业广告感、元素堆砌、过度装饰、脏旧纸张、随机噪点、塑料感、3D CGI、玻璃材质、霓虹色、Logo、水印、编号、星芒装饰。

prompts.text:
Prompt:

[POSTER THEME]: {fill in the theme}
[MAIN TITLE]: {fill in the title}
[TOP SECTION]: {portrait / object archive / typography / image}
[MIDDLE SECTION]: {information band / typography / image / transition}
[BOTTOM SECTION]: {landscape / hero object / second portrait / typography}
[COLOR PALETTE]: {fill in the palette}
[VISUAL STYLE]: {editorial / museum / photography exhibition / cultural poster}
[ASPECT RATIO]: 9:16

Create a sophisticated vertical editorial poster built around a clear three-part composition: top, middle, and bottom.

Each section must have a distinct visual role, but the final poster should feel like one continuous design rather than three stacked rectangular panels.

Use strong differences in scale, image density, typography, and negative space to establish hierarchy.

The top section should create the first visual anchor through a bold image, oversized typography, or a strong subject.

The middle section should act as the structural hinge of the composition. It can use a title, information field, narrow panoramic image, color band, or typography layer to connect the upper and lower sections.

The bottom section should provide a second visual weight or spatial conclusion through a landscape, object, secondary portrait, or oversized type.

Avoid rigid card-like boundaries. Let selected elements cross between sections through masking, overlap, irregular silhouettes, transparency, atmospheric transitions, foreground/background relationships, or typography extending beyond its original area.

Typography must actively participate in the composition rather than simply sit on top of the image. Allow large letterforms to be cropped by the page, partially hidden behind subjects, overlap imagery, or interact with negative space.

Use a strong editorial hierarchy:
one dominant title,
one clear secondary information layer,
and small meaningful metadata such as dates, venue, category, or curatorial text.

Small text should feel like real exhibition or editorial information, not decorative filler.

Keep some areas intentionally quiet. Do not fill every empty space.

The first read should communicate the main visual structure immediately.
The second read should reveal the interaction between type and imagery.
The third read should reveal the smaller information and details.

Maintain a refined contemporary poster aesthetic with strong typography, deliberate cropping, controlled information density, clean print texture, and professional editorial spacing.

生成一张具有强烈编辑设计感和文化展览气质的高密度海报。核心目标不是减少信息，而是通过明确的视觉层级，让大型中文、异形主图、线条、图形、小型信息和背景纹理同时存在，形成“乱中有序”的版式效果。

先确定 1 个绝对主视觉锚点，再设置 2–3 个次级视觉锚点。主视觉可以采用异形裁切、轮廓窗口、局部破框或图像融合，不要只是普通矩形照片。大型中文标题必须真正参与构图，可从边缘压入、局部裁切、与主图遮挡穿插，成为版面结构的一部分，而不是简单贴在图片旁边。

信息密度保持中高，加入中英文标题、日期、机构、短说明、竖排文字、局部图例、数据、坐标、线条或小型图像切片，但不同元素必须具有明显尺度差异。超大字、中号标题和极小信息之间形成强烈字号跳跃，不要所有文字大小接近，也不要把内容平均分散到整个画面。

整张海报只使用一套与主题相关的辅助视觉语言。例如城市主题使用路线与街区图形，观念主题使用流线与图像残片，自然主题使用植物线稿与标本信息，气象主题使用等压线、风向和雷达图。不要同时堆入多套无关装饰。

背景也必须参与设计，可以加入极淡的纹样、地图、结构图、档案文字、数据残影或材料纹理，让留白区域有内容，但背景层必须明显弱于主体。

允许文字压图、图像破框、线条跨区、小图切片叠入版面，通过局部遮挡和不完全对齐增加后现代编辑感，但所有元素必须围绕同一个视觉中心组织。整体保持 1 个主锚点 + 2–3 个次锚点，避免真正散乱。

色彩控制在 3–5 个主要颜色，建立明确色彩立场，可使用高饱和主色搭配黑白，也可以采用统一单色体系。不要让多个高饱和色平均竞争。

阅读顺序应为：第一眼看到主体和大型压角文字；第二眼发现异形图像、图形与线条关系；第三眼再阅读日期、说明、数据和边缘信息。

最终效果像成熟的文化展览海报、设计学院视觉或编辑类出版物：信息丰富、层级复杂、局部碰撞，但缩小后依然拥有清晰视觉中心。不要做成信息图PPT，也不要为了“复杂”随机填满画面。

Prompt:

Create a bold editorial campaign poster where oversized typography acts as a transformation zone that changes the subject or product as it passes through.

Brand: [BRAND NAME]
Product / Campaign: [PRODUCT OR CAMPAIGN]
Main Word: [SHORT WORD]
Subject: [PERSON / PRODUCT / BOTH]
Transformation: [MODE / TEMPERATURE / ENERGY / GROWTH / OTHER]
Before State: [DESCRIBE INITIAL STATE]
After State: [DESCRIBE FINAL STATE]
Main Color: [COLOR]
Accent Color: [COLOR]
Aspect Ratio: [9:16]

Use realistic commercial photography, oversized typography, high-contrast colors, and contemporary editorial design.

Make the main word extremely large and clearly divide the transformation into three stages: Before → Transition → After

The subject must remain the same person or same product throughout the image. Keep its identity, structure, pose, clothing shape, packaging, and proportions consistent while only the intended state changes.

Let the transformation happen specifically inside the typography. For example:

 MODE: change colors, materials, or visual styling.
 TEMPERATURE: shift from dry and warm to condensation, frost, and cold surfaces.
 ENERGY: increase brightness, illuminated accents, or power indicators.
 GROWTH: let color, plants, or organic forms gradually emerge from the letterforms.

Create clear foreground–subject–background interaction, with parts of the typography passing behind and in front of the subject.

Use one strong color system before the transformation and a contrasting state after it, while keeping the transition controlled and readable.

Add only a few meaningful campaign details such as the brand name, product name, slogan, specifications, or small editorial labels.

The final image should feel like a finished campaign key visual where the typography visibly causes the transformation.

【场景】：城市夜色 / 玻璃温室 / 夏末麦田 / 酒店长廊 / 其他场景
【服装】：简洁轻盈的夏季服装
【花束】：花材、颜色与形态
【主色调】：场景主色 + 花束点缀色
【情绪】：流逝 / 静谧 / 盛放 / 余温 / 其他
【中文标题】：稍纵即逝的烂漫
【英文副标题】：BEFORE IT FADES

整体采用写实 Editorial Photography × 情绪艺术海报视觉语言，不是普通人物写真或商业广告。

人物保持真实自然的五官、皮肤纹理和身体比例。核心使用“局部清晰 + 动态残影”的摄影方式：人物身体、肩颈、手部和部分花束保持相对清晰；头发、脸部边缘、衣摆或动作方向产生自然的慢速快门 motion blur、轻微双重曝光和时间错位效果。

不要整个人平均模糊。脸部主体仍然需要可辨认，只让局部五官、发丝或轮廓产生方向明确的残影，让画面像同时记录了两个非常接近的时间节点。

花束作为情绪视觉锚点，中心花朵相对清晰，外围花瓣、枝叶可以出现少量动态拖影。花束颜色与场景形成明确的冷暖或明暗对比。

背景根据场景产生不同的流动效果，例如交通灯光横向拉丝、植物前景掠过、麦田和裙摆随风流动、走廊灯光形成时间残影。背景需要有运动和空气感，但不要抢过人物。

构图保持不完全对称和自然留白，人物放在画面一侧，另一侧留给标题与环境。加入克制的中文竖排标题和小号英文副标题，使用现代宋体 / 细衬线字体，让部分发丝、光影或环境残影轻微穿过文字区域，使 Typography 与摄影自然融合。

整体低饱和、电影感、真实、诗意、有情绪张力。画面既要有人物美感，也要有时间正在流逝的感觉。

生成一张具有强动势和成熟 Editorial Design 气质的「中轴夹景」文化海报。

先建立一条明确、稳定的中央硬轴，可以是船身、竹脊、箭矢、器物结构或其他纵向主体；再让左右两侧的重复元素、弧线、斜线或波纹共同把视觉力量压向中央。

左右元素不只是装饰，而要真正参与方向感和节奏。可以使用桨阵、骨架、弓身、声波、羽翼、杆件等形成连续视觉序列，通过重复、放射、倾斜和尺度变化制造动势。

画面要有一个非常清楚的第一视觉大形：中央硬轴 + 两侧方向性结构。左右视觉重量保持平衡，但不要机械镜像，允许角度、尺度、材质和节奏存在变化。

Typography 根据主体方向重新设计，可以横跨结构、贴近硬轴、沿大形排布或局部错位，不要固定使用四字纵排、巨大单字居中或同一种标题模板。

可加入一个很小的结构研究模块，例如动作阶段、受力、波纹、骨架或路径示意，面积控制在 5%–7%，增加“设计研究感”，但不要做成 PPT 或教学图。

色彩控制在 3–5 个主要颜色，使用明确的大色域和强主体反差。

第一眼看到大形和动势，第二眼看到中轴和标题，第三眼发现两侧元素如何共同制造方向与张力。

避免：机械对称、重复元素完全复制、主体过小、方向混乱、多个视觉中心、复杂技术参数、PPT 信息框、随机装饰线、过度做旧、斑驳噪点和低完成度 AI 海报感。

For interlacing, use real over-and-under relationships between continuous bands so the visible foreground segments collectively form the letters.

Keep all perspective, depth, occlusion, material behavior and surface continuity physically believable. From other viewpoints, the typography should partially break apart and reveal the actual spatial construction.

Use bold geometric sans-serif letterforms, a restrained architectural environment and a controlled palette with strong graphic contrast.

If a person is included, keep them small and use them mainly as a scale reference, with realistic foreground and background occlusion.

prompts.text:
Nano banana V2.1 on Flow. 

System prompt : 
HUMAN PORTRAIT DIRECTOR
ROLE

Translate user briefs into production ready image generation prompts for photographic portraits. Prioritize authentic skin anatomy, subtle facial expression, directional lighting, and clear focal hierarchy.
Support individual portraits, paired portraits, environmental portraits, and multi image character series. Strictly follow all user specifications for subject identity, age, wardrobe, environment, lighting, aspect ratio, and target model format.

REFERENCE HANDLING

 * Attribute Isolation: Distinguish style references from identity, pose, wardrobe, lighting, and composition. Apply only the parameters assigned to each specific reference. Style references govern photographic treatment only; they do not dictate subject identity, garments, or layout.

 * Artifact Exclusion: Disregard UI overlays, watermarks, crop borders, and annotations present in reference images unless explicitly requested.
 * Missing Assets: If a referenced file is unavailable and essential to generation, request clarification rather than guessing.

FACIAL GEOMETRY AND EXPRESSION

 * Underlying Structure: Establish cranial anatomy, cheek volume, jaw contour, orbital depth, nose bridge, lips, and hairline before adding micro-detail. Maintain organic asymmetry and believable proportions.

 * Mature Anatomy: Distribute aging characteristics naturally across facial planes (brow laxity, periorbital lines, nasolabial folds, jawline softening). Avoid exaggerating every aging artifact on a single face.

 * Observable Expression: Define visible muscular movement rather than subjective mood adjectives. Specify gaze vector, eyelid aperture, brow tension, lip closure, and head angle.
SKIN AND SURFACE OPTICS
 * Scale Hierarchy: Describe skin across macro volume, anatomical folds, and micro-surface variation according to camera distance and framing.
 * Texture Distribution: Keep skin texture non-uniform. Forehead creases follow the frontal muscle, crow's feet radiate outward, and nasolabial folds follow facial contours. Pore visibility varies naturally across the T-zone and cheeks.
 * Material Physics: Distinguish surface relief from pigmentation. Treat freckles, lentigines, and minor vascular flush as pigmentation variations rather than physical indentations. Specify realistic specular response: diffuse matte planes along the perimeter with soft specular sheen across the bridge and cheeks.

 * Optical Attenuation: Micro-detail resolves only where the primary light and focal plane intersect. Shadows and optical defocus must naturally soften surface detail.

 * Anti Artifact Guardrails: Avoid waxy smoothing, synthetic pore overlays, over carved wrinkles, high frequency digital sharpening, and uniform oily shine across the face.

EYES, HAIR, AND CONTACT POINTS

 * Ocular Optics: Make the eyes the primary focal anchor when visible. Specify natural limbal rings, iris depth, moist lower lid margins, and precise catchlights consistent with the key light source.

 * Hair Dynamics: Define hair as volumetric masses and layered groupings accented by broken strands and organic flyaways. Avoid wire-like rendering, edge halos, or uniform strand density.

 * Physical Contact: When hands touch the face or neck, specify the hand, finger posture, contact point, and tissue compression. Match hand scale, vascularity, skin tone, and age characteristics to the face.

OPTICS AND COMPOSITION

 * Framing and Stance: Define camera framing (close-up, medium portrait, environmental portrait) and cranial angle (frontal, three quarter, profile). Decouple ocular gaze direction from head orientation.

 * Focal Length: Use short telephoto perspectives (typically 85mm full-frame equivalent) to ensure natural facial compression and prevent wide-angle optical distortion.

 * Depth of Field: Specify depth of field directly. Anchor critical focus on the nearest eye, allowing ears, rear hairline, wardrobe, and background to roll off into progressive optical blur. Maintain focal coherence across multiple subjects.

LIGHTING SETUP

 * Key Architecture: Anchor the scene with a dominant primary source (such as diffused north-facing window light or a large studio softbox). Specify source angle, elevation, and falloff relative to the camera axis.
 * Shadow Modulation: Use directional modeling to define facial planes while preserving gradated penumbras. Maintain ambient fill control: avoid muddy shadow crush, unmotivated rim lights, blown specular highlights, or conflicting catchlights.
 * Occlusion: Ensure hair, wardrobe, and hands cast accurate contact shadows across adjacent surfaces.

COLOR, WARDROBE, AND ENVIRONMENT

 * Color Grading: Preserve authentic skin undertones. Maintain controlled tonal contrast against subdued, neutral, or low-key backgrounds. Avoid global orange/teal grading or uniform color casts.
 * Wardrobe Realism: Specify realistic fabric properties (textile weave, weight, drape, seam structure, and subtle wear).

 * Background Depth: Keep backgrounds clean, contextual, and unobtrusive. Separate the subject using tonal contrast, selective lighting, and optical bokeh rather than decorative clutter.

 * Dynamic Range: Preserve midtone detail, highlight retention, and clean shadow separation. Do not use exaggerated clarity filters, HDR halos, or crushed blacks.

SERIES CONTINUITY

 * Independence: Generate complete, standalone prompts per frame. Do not format outputs as contact sheets or multi-panel grids unless explicitly directed.
 * Character Consistency: For consistent identity across a series, lock core facial geometry, eye shape, and defining traits. Vary only pose, framing, wardrobe, or light.
 * Cohort Diversity: For distinct subjects within a shared series, vary underlying bone structure and features while maintaining consistent optical and lighting parameters.

PROMPT ARCHITECTURE

 * Clause Sequence: Structure prompts logically: Subject and Demographics -> Framing and Camera Angle -> Pose and Muscular Expression -> Wardrobe and Props -> Key and Ambient Lighting -> Surface Optics and Focus Roll-Off -> Background and Atmosphere -> Technical Parameters.

 * Anti-Slop Directive: Exclude buzzwords such as "photorealistic", "hyperrealistic", "masterpiece", "award-winning", "8K resolution", "unreal engine", or publication names. Replace subjective praise with concrete photographic descriptors: lens focal length, aperture setting, lighting geometry, and surface physics.
 * Token Economy: Keep standard prompts compact and information-dense (approximately 150 to 220 words). Every sentence must specify a visible physical property or mitigate a generative failure mode.

PLATFORM AND SYNTAX HANDLING

 * Parameter Compliance: When targeting Midjourney, append only valid, verified flags (such as --ar, --stylize, --v) at the end of the prompt. Do not fabricate seed numbers, personalization hashes, or style reference codes.
 * Schema Adherence: When JSON or YAML output is requested, output strict, valid schemas without inline comments, markdown wrappers inside keys, or trailing commas.
 * Multilingual Terminology: When non-English output is requested, use verified photographic and optical terminology in the target language.

OUTPUT PROTOCOL

 * Return strictly the finished prompt text (or numbered list for multiple prompts) without conversational preamble, sign-offs, or meta-commentary unless requested.
 * Use direct language with zero em dashes, zero decorative markdown wrappers, and zero vague filler.

Prompt : Create a visually stunning 20-second surreal science-fiction mystery film using the four supplied images as environmental references. Maintain the same abandoned motel, dense turquoise-green fog, glowing orange-red neon, vintage CRT monitors, hanging cables, and atmospheric analog technology throughout.
SHOT 01 | 00:00–00:02 | THE MOTEL
Extreme wide cinematic shot. A solitary man in a long dark coat approaches an isolated roadside motel through thick rolling cyan fog. The red MOTEL sign flickers overhead. Wet asphalt reflects the neon. Slow low-angle dolly forward.
SHOT 02 | 00:02–00:04 | THE CALL
Interior macro close-up. A dusty black rotary telephone suddenly rings on an abandoned reception desk. Its cable lies unplugged beside it. A small red indicator light blinks in perfect rhythm with the ringing.
SHOT 03 | 00:04–00:06 | THE INSTRUCTION
Tight profile shot of the man lifting the telephone receiver. Through crackling analog static, a distorted recording of his own voice whispers: "Channel nine." His eyes slowly shift toward a glowing terminal in the darkness.
SHOT 04 | 00:06–00:08 | THE FREQUENCY
Extreme close-up of his fingers rotating a large metallic tuning dial. The terminal displays "CH 09". Its screen erupts with white static, then reveals a quiet, sunlit road outside the motel. Warm golden light spills onto his fingers.
SHOT 05 | 00:08–00:10 | THE IMPOSSIBLE WINDOW
A dramatic wide shot reveals an enormous wall of stacked CRT televisions. Every screen shows dense blue-green fog except one central television displaying brilliant golden daylight. The man stands silhouetted before the glowing screens. Slow symmetrical camera push-in.
SHOT 06 | 00:10–00:12 | THE DISCOVERY
Side-profile close-up. The man gently places his palm against the sunlit television. Instead of solid glass, the screen ripples like liquid mercury. Warm sunlight illuminates his face while the surrounding room remains cold and green.
SHOT 07 | 00:12–00:14 | THE CROSSING
Smooth over-the-shoulder tracking shot. The man steps carefully through the glowing television surface. The golden light envelops him. The surrounding CRT screens flicker simultaneously as he disappears into the image.
SHOT 08 | 00:14–00:17 | THE ESCAPE
Cut to the exterior. The man emerges onto the empty motel road, now bathed in beautiful golden morning sunlight. The thick fog slowly dissolves. He looks at the open sky, visibly relieved. The camera gently orbits him as natural birdsong replaces the electrical humming.
SHOT 09 | 00:17–00:20 | THE TWIST
The camera suddenly pulls backward, faster and faster. The beautiful sunlit road shrinks into the curved glass of a vintage CRT television. We are still inside the original dark control room. The same man's silhouette sits motionless in a chair, watching his own escape on Channel 09.
The screen flickers once.
Cut to black.
VISUAL LANGUAGE:
Photorealistic 35mm film, vintage anamorphic lenses, dense volumetric fog, deep emerald shadows, icy cyan highlights, orange-red neon, physical CRT bloom, subtle halation, wet reflective textures, realistic analog machinery. Precise cinematic blocking, striking silhouettes, slow controlled camera movement, seamless transitions, no artificial-looking CGI.
SOUND DESIGN:
Wind through deserted streets, rotary telephone ringing, magnetic tape hiss, electronic frequency sweeps, low atmospheric synthesizer drone, gentle birdsong during the apparent escape, and a final single CRT shutdown click.
CONTINUITY:
One adult male protagonist, consistent dark coat and hairstyle. No children, violence, injury, dangerous actions, or threatening figures. No narration or subtitles. Only minimal diegetic screen text. Exactly nine shots, totaling 20 seconds.

【作者评论区补充】

prompts.text:
I asked Nano Banana to visualize 4 manga about devils. 

Prompt: 

2x2 grid, 16:9, do this for 4 famous mangas about demons  TOPIC=[...] 
 
Create a minimalist black-and-white semantic wordmark for TOPIC. 
 
Infer automatically: 
 
DISPLAY_WORD = 
derive the shortest powerful word, title, name, or concept associated with TOPIC 
 
DUAL_FORCES = 
infer two opposing, complementary, mirrored, or relational ideas within TOPIC 
 
LEFT_SYMBOL = 
infer the simplest recognizable silhouette representing DUAL_FORCES[0] 
 
RIGHT_SYMBOL = 
infer the simplest recognizable silhouette representing DUAL_FORCES[1] 
 
TYPOGRAPHY = 
custom monumental display lettering designed specifically to accommodate those silhouettes 
 
Construct one unified black graphic where: 
 
- DISPLAY_WORD is immediately readable 
- LEFT_SYMBOL is fused into the left boundary of the first letter 
- RIGHT_SYMBOL is fused into the right boundary of the final letter 
- symbols face inward, outward, oppose, reflect, confront, or complement each other depending on TOPIC 
- black letterforms and symbolic silhouettes share continuous edges 
- white negative space separates and reveals forms 
- typography is sculpted around symbolic contours rather than having symbols pasted beside it 
 
STYLE: 
pure black ink 
warm white or clean white background 
flat vector graphic 
no gradients 
no shadows 
no texture 
no extra illustration 
strong horizontal composition 
editorial-logo precision 
 
FAR VIEW = readable word 
MID VIEW = unusual custom typography 
NEAR VIEW = hidden semantic silhouettes 
 
Do not hard-code faces, profiles, the word TRUTH, symmetry type, serif style, or subject matter. 
Infer everything from TOPIC.

【作者评论区补充】
These prompts are amazing because I work on them for a topic but then you give them a completely unrelated topic and AI gets very creative!  I have to play with it more!

prompts.text:
提示词：

【主题】：
【中文标题】：
【英文标题】：
【核心主体】：
【左右关系】：巨物压场 / 图像窄带 × 宽文字场 / 主体 × 档案 / 图像越界 / 密集 × 留白 / 其他
【左侧内容】：
【右侧内容】：
【跨界元素】：器物轮廓 / 枝叶 / 大字 / 线稿 / 纹样 / 其他
【主色调】：
【强调色】：
【日期 / 场馆】：
【画面比例】：9:16

生成一张高审美、高信息密度的东方文化展览海报，采用「左右构图 / 非对称双区构图」。

左右不要 50 / 50 平均切开，根据主体体量、文字密度和留白关系灵活使用 35 / 65、40 / 60、45 / 55 等比例。重点不是两侧面积相等，而是让图像重量、Typography 和信息密度达到视觉平衡。

根据主题灵活选择不同方式：

巨物压场：一侧放大尺度器物、文物或艺术对象，允许大胆裁切，占据主要视觉重量；另一侧通过标题、英文、小字、结构线稿和展讯建立阅读层级。

图像窄带 × 宽文字场：一侧使用修长古画、摄影或纹样切片，另一侧保留更大的纸面与 Typography。图像中的枝叶、飞鸟、云气或主体轮廓可主动越出画芯进入文字区。

主体 × 档案：一侧保持单一强主体，另一侧组合器型线稿、材质微距、拓片、纹样研究、尺寸、年代和少量说明文字，形成艺术图录感。

密集 × 留白：一侧通过图像、档案碎片和研究内容形成高密度视觉，另一侧保持大面积控制过的留白，只使用少量大字和关键展讯。留白不能只是“没有内容”，要通过字距、细线、位置和比例被精确设计。

左右边界不要过于机械。可以让器物边缘、大字、花枝、纹样或研究线条跨过分界约 3%–10%，把两侧重新连接起来，但避免随意拼贴。

Typography 必须根据每张画面的主体重新设计。可以使用超大单字、两字错位、完整横排标题、中等尺度标题、跨栏文字或局部反色。坚持“大字很大、小字很小”的尺度反差，减少无意义的中号字。不要固定使用四字纵排，也不要重复“两字横排 + 两字竖排”的模板。

信息密度参考成熟博物馆海报、Japanese Editorial Design 和 Art Catalogue。可加入英文副标题、年代、材质、工艺、场馆、日期、策展短句，以及 1–3 个与主题直接相关的研究节点，例如器型线稿、釉面微距、古画材料、纹样拓片、石纹研究或局部放大。

这些辅助信息必须服务主题，不要为了“显得专业”而堆随机小字。

色彩控制在 3–5 个主要颜色。优先使用骨白、墨黑、青瓷绿、石青石绿、深灰、赭色等克制色彩，再加入一个明确但面积很小的朱砂红或其他强调色。纸面保持干净，不使用脏黄仿古滤镜。

第一眼看到大型主体与左右重量关系；第二眼看到标题和主要色块；第三眼发现器物、古画或枝叶如何突破左右边界；最后再阅读材质、结构、年代与展览档案。

核心原则：一边负责压住视觉，一边负责承接阅读；留白也是重量，信息密度也是重量；左右不相等，但整体必须平衡。

整体要求：9:16，高清、清晰、纸面干净、主体质感真实、Typography 锐利、细线与小字尽可能清楚，信息丰富但不乱，具有成熟博物馆海报和艺术出版物完成度。

prompts.text:
Prompt:

Create a bold commercial campaign poster where oversized typography behaves like a real physical object and actively interacts with the subject.

Brand: [BRAND NAME]
Product: [PRODUCT]
Main Word: [SHORT WORD]
Subject: [PERSON / PRODUCT / BOTH]
Motion Type: [SWING / FLEX / FLIP / ROLL / OTHER]
Main Color: [COLOR]
Accent Color: [COLOR]
Aspect Ratio: [9:16]

Use realistic commercial photography, oversized typography, strong perspective, vivid color contrast, and contemporary editorial design.

Make the main word extremely large and give it one clear physical behavior:

 SWING: suspend the letters and let them move like swinging gates while the subject passes between them.
 FLEX: let the letter surface bend smoothly under the subject’s weight, then visibly rebound.
 FLIP: rotate different letters around simple pivot axes and reveal a contrasting back surface.
 ROLL: turn a round letter into a rolling typographic form that moves through the scene and interacts with real wheels or objects.

The subject must physically react to the typography through stepping, dodging, balancing, riding, or making contact with it.

Keep the typography clearly readable. Use clean matte surfaces, even colors, sharp edges, and controlled depth. Avoid rough concrete, distressed textures, scratches, dirt, random noise, and heavy 3D architecture.

All motion arcs, guide lines, callout lines, and curves must be smooth, continuous, and clearly rendered.

Keep people highly realistic with natural anatomy, believable proportions, real skin texture, controlled highlights, detailed hair, and authentic clothing materials. Avoid waxy skin, oily reflections, CGI appearance, distorted limbs, oversized hands or feet, and extreme wide angle deformation.

Use one dominant high impact color, one contrasting accent color, and black or white for balance. Add only a few meaningful campaign details such as the brand name, product name, slogan, and 2 to 3 short feature callouts.

The final image should feel like a finished campaign key visual where typography, motion, and the subject behave as one physical system.

Avoid generic subject plus big text layouts, random motion effects, broken lines, unreadable typography, cluttered UI, rough materials, unrealistic anatomy, and meaningless filler text.

title: PERSON / PRODUCT / BOTH

生成一张具有强空间感和成熟 Editorial Design 气质的「中轴夹景」文化海报。

核心不是简单把两个主体左右对称摆放，而是利用器物、山势、飞檐、建筑等主体自身的**轮廓、方向和透视关系**，共同围出清晰的中央空间，让“空间本身”成为构图的一部分。

根据主题选择不同夹景方式：

扇面、圆盘等弧形主体，可以利用弧线和放射结构向中央聚拢；
山体、岩壁、树木等自然形态，可以通过不规则轮廓夹出水路、天空或远景；
飞檐、屋顶等建筑构件，可以利用倾斜方向共同托住月亮、太阳或标题；
门、墙、廊道等空间元素，可以通过透视线向中央收束，形成明显纵深。

左右视觉重量保持平衡，但不要机械镜像。允许主体在大小、材质、角度、颜色和裁切方式上明显不同，只要它们共同强化中轴。

中轴不一定放满文字，可以是一轮月、一条河、一段天空、一个人物、一个透视通道，甚至大面积留白。让中央内容足够简单，才能突出两侧轮廓形成的“夹景”。

Typography 根据每张画面的几何结构重新设计，可以使用超大单字、横向标题、左右拆字、贴边排版、跨越留白或沿结构方向排字。避免每张都使用相同的四字纵排，或固定“两字横排 + 两字竖排”的模板。

信息集中在 2–3 个区域，可加入少量建筑剖面、山势线稿、扇骨结构、透视辅助线等研究元素，但必须服务主题，不要做成 PPT 信息图。

整体视觉方向：

Museum Exhibition Poster × Contemporary Editorial Graphic Design × East Asian Cultural Visual

色彩控制在 3–5 个主要颜色，使用明确的大色域和强对比。第一眼看到主体轮廓和中央空间，第二眼读到标题，第三眼发现弧线、山势或透视如何共同建立中轴。

整体要求：高清、干净、结构明确、空间感强、信息丰富但不杂乱。避免机械对称、主体过小、中央塞满文字、固定标题模板、透视混乱、无意义装饰线、脏旧纹理、模糊细节和低完成度 AI 海报感。

Prompt:

Brand: 
Product / Campaign: 
Main Word:
Subject: 
Action: 
Motion Direction: 
Product / Key Object: 
Main Color: 
Accent Color: 
Campaign Details: 
Aspect Ratio: [9:16]

Create a bold commercial campaign poster where the entire composition follows one clear direction of motion.

Capture the subject at a strong peak-action moment with believable anatomy, balance, weight, and momentum. Hair, clothing, limbs, equipment, and body posture should naturally follow the same movement.

Make the oversized main word a major part of this motion system rather than static background text. Arrange, rotate, curve, shift, or offset the typography according to the chosen movement direction.

For circular motion, let the letters wrap around the subject.
For diving or diagonal motion, stretch the type along the body trajectory.
For turning motion, curve the typography through perspective.
For sliding motion, shift large sections of the letters horizontally.

Keep the main word large, bold, and clearly readable even when transformed.

Create controlled foreground–subject–background layering. Some parts of the typography may sit behind the subject while selected sections move in front, making the person and type feel connected within the same space.

Use perspective and scale to strengthen the direction of motion, but avoid extreme distortion that damages the subject or product.

Use one high-saturation dominant color with one strong contrasting accent, plus black, white, or metallic neutrals. Keep the palette bold and controlled.

Add 2–3 compact information areas with meaningful campaign details such as product name, weight, material, performance feature, specification, or slogan, plus a clean footer.

The visual hierarchy should be: dynamic subject → motion direction → oversized typography → product → campaign details

Keep people, hands, hair, equipment, wheels, boards, gloves, and other products realistic and structurally correct.

The final image should feel like a finished high-energy editorial campaign — colorful, directional, dimensional, dynamic, and immediately readable in a social feed.
